sentences.zh: 【唐紀六十六】起上章執徐，盡強圉大淵獻，凡八年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 66] From the year shangzhang zhixu through qiangyu dayuanxian, eight years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 66] Covering the eight years from the cyclical year shangzhang zhixu through qiangyu dayuanxian.

sentences.zh: 懿宗昭聖恭惠孝皇帝上咸通元年（

translations.literal: Above: Emperor Yizong, the Sagely, Respectful, and Gracious Filial Emperor; first year of Xiantong (
translations.idiomatic: Reign of Emperor Yizong of Tang — first year of Xiantong (

sentences.zh: 庚辰，公元八六零年）

translations.literal: gengchen, the year 860 CE)
translations.idiomatic: gengchen, 860 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙卯，浙東軍與裘甫戰於桐柏觀前，范居植死，劉勍僅以身免。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on the day yimao, the Zhedong army fought Qiu Fu before Tongbai Abbey; Fan Juzhi was killed, and Liu Xin barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first month's yimao day, the Zhedong army clashed with Qiu Fu before Tongbai Abbey. Fan Juzhi was killed, and Liu Xin barely got away alive.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，甫帥其徒千餘人陷剡縣，開府庫，募壯士，眾至數千人。

translations.literal: On the day yichou, Fu led more than a thousand followers to seize Shan County, opened the government treasury, recruited strong men, and his force grew to several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Fu led over a thousand men to take Shan County, threw open the treasury, and recruited fighters until his band numbered several thousand.

sentences.zh: 越州大恐。

translations.literal: Yue Prefecture was greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Panic spread through Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時二浙久安，人不習戰，甲兵朽鈍，見卒不滿三百，鄭祗德更募新卒以益之。

translations.literal: At the time the two Zhe regions had long been at peace; the people were unused to war, armor and weapons were rotten and dull, and the troops on hand numbered fewer than three hundred. Zheng Qide recruited new soldiers to augment them.
translations.idiomatic: The two Zhe circuits had known peace for so long that the populace was unaccustomed to fighting; arms were rusted and blunt, and fewer than three hundred soldiers were on hand. Zheng Qide raised fresh recruits to bolster the garrison.

sentences.zh: 軍吏受賂，率皆得孱弱者。

translations.literal: The army officers took bribes and for the most part obtained weaklings.
translations.idiomatic: Officers took bribes and, as a rule, enrolled only the feeblest men they could find.

sentences.zh: 祗德遣子將沈君縱、副將張公署、望海鎮將李珪將新卒五百擊裘甫。

translations.literal: Qide sent the subordinate commander Shen Junzong, the deputy commander Zhang Gongshu, and the Wanghai garrison commander Li Gui to lead five hundred new recruits against Qiu Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Qide dispatched subordinate commander Shen Junzong, deputy commander Zhang Gongshu, and Wanghai garrison commander Li Gui with five hundred new troops to attack Qiu Fu.

sentences.zh: 二月，辛卯，與甫戰於剡西，賊設伏於三溪之南，而陳於三溪之北，壅溪上流，使可涉。

translations.literal: Second month, on the day xinmao, they fought Fu west of Shan. The rebels set an ambush south of Sanxi and drew up in battle order north of Sanxi, damming the upper stream so that the river could be forded.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinmao, they met Fu west of Shan. The rebels hid troops south of Sanxi while forming a line north of the stream, damming the upper waters so the crossing looked shallow.

sentences.zh: 既戰，陽敗走，官軍追之，半涉，決壅，水大至，官軍大敗，三將皆死，官軍幾盡。

translations.literal: Once battle was joined, they feigned defeat and fled; the government troops pursued. When the troops were halfway across, the dam was breached, a great flood came down, and the government army was utterly defeated. All three commanders died, and the army was nearly wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: After the fighting began, the rebels pretended to flee; the government force gave chase. Midstream, the dam was cut and a torrent swept down. The army was routed, all three commanders were killed, and almost no one escaped.

sentences.zh: 於是山海諸盜及它道無賴亡命之徒，四面雲集，眾至三萬，分為三十二隊。

translations.literal: Thereupon bandits of the mountains and sea and ruffians and fugitives from other routes gathered from all sides like clouds; the host reached thirty thousand and was divided into thirty-two companies.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits from coast and hill country, along with outlaws and fugitives from every quarter, flocked in until the host numbered thirty thousand, organized into thirty-two companies.

sentences.zh: 其小帥有謀略者推劉暀，勇力推劉慶、劉從簡。

translations.literal: Among the minor chiefs, those with stratagems acclaimed Liu Chang; for courage and strength they acclaimed Liu Qing and Liu Congjian.
translations.idiomatic: The minor leaders chose Liu Chang for counsel and Liu Qing and Liu Congjian for raw fighting power.

sentences.zh: 群盜皆遙通書幣，求屬麾下。

translations.literal: Bandit groups everywhere sent letters and gifts from afar, seeking to place themselves under his command.
translations.idiomatic: Bandit bands far and wide sent messages and gifts, asking to serve under him.

sentences.zh: 甫自稱天下都知兵馬使，改元曰羅平，鑄印曰天平。

translations.literal: Fu styled himself Commander-in-Chief of All Armies Under Heaven, changed the era name to Luoping, and cast a seal reading Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: Fu proclaimed himself supreme commander of all armies under heaven, adopted the era name Luoping, and cast a seal inscribed Tianping.

sentences.zh: 大聚資糧，購良工，治器械，聲震中原。

translations.literal: He amassed great stores of provisions, hired skilled craftsmen, and prepared weapons; his fame shook the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: He stockpiled grain, hired skilled artisans, and armed his forces until his renown echoed across the heartland.

sentences.zh: 丙申，葬聖武獻文孝皇帝於貞陵，廟號宣宗。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen, the Sagely Martial and Literary Filial Emperor was buried at Zhenling; his temple name is Xuanzong.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, the late emperor was buried at Zhenling with the temple name Xuanzong.

sentences.zh: 丙午，白敏中入朝，墜陛，傷腰，肩輿以歸。

translations.literal: On the day bingwu, Bai Minzhong entered court, fell from the steps, injured his waist, and was carried home in a sedan chair.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Bai Minzhong came to court, fell on the palace steps, hurt his back, and was borne home in a litter.

sentences.zh: 鄭祗德累表告急，且求救於鄰道。

translations.literal: Zheng Qide repeatedly memorialized in urgent alarm and also sought rescue from neighboring circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Qide sent repeated urgent memorials and appealed to neighboring circuits for help.

sentences.zh: 浙西遣牙將凌茂貞將四百人、宣歙遣牙將白琮將三百人赴之。

translations.literal: Zhexi sent the adjutant Ling Maozhen with four hundred men, and Xuan-She sent the adjutant Bai Cong with three hundred men to go to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Zhexi dispatched adjutant Ling Maozhen with four hundred troops, and Xuan-She sent adjutant Bai Cong with three hundred.

sentences.zh: 祗德始令屯郭門及東小江，尋復召還府中以自衛。

translations.literal: Qide at first ordered them to encamp at the city gate and at East Xiaojiang, but soon recalled them to the prefectural seat for his own protection.
translations.idiomatic: Qide first posted them at the city gate and East Xiaojiang, then pulled them back into the prefectural compound for his own protection.

sentences.zh: 祗德饋之，比度支常饋多十三倍，而宣、潤將士猶以為不足。

translations.literal: Qide supplied them with provisions thirteen times the usual allotment from the Ministry of Revenue, yet the officers and soldiers of Xuan and Run still deemed it insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Qide provisioned them at thirteen times the usual Ministry of Revenue rate, yet the Xuan and Run troops still complained it was not enough.

sentences.zh: 宣、潤將士請土軍為導，以與賊戰。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers of Xuan and Run asked that local troops serve as guides so they could fight the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuan and Run contingents asked for local guides to lead them against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 諸將或稱病，或陽墜馬，其肯行者必先邀職級，竟不果遣。

translations.literal: Some commanders claimed illness, others pretended to fall from their horses; those willing to go first demanded promotions in rank. In the end none were sent out.
translations.idiomatic: Some officers pleaded illness, others staged falls from their horses; those willing to march demanded promotions first. In the end, no one was sent to fight.

sentences.zh: 賊游騎至平水東小江，城中士民儲舟裹糧，夜坐待旦，各謀逃潰。

translations.literal: Rebel scouting horsemen reached Ping River and East Xiaojiang; within the city soldiers and civilians stored boats and packed grain, sitting up through the night until dawn, each plotting flight and dispersal.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel scouts reached Ping River and East Xiaojiang. Inside the city, people packed boats and grain, sat up all night, and each made plans to flee.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知祗德懦怯，議選武將代之。

translations.literal: The court knew Qide was timid and cowardly and debated selecting a military commander to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Qide was timid and ineffectual, the court debated replacing him with a fighting general.

sentences.zh: 夏侯孜曰：「浙東山海幽阻，可以計取，難以力攻。

translations.literal: Xiahou Zi said: "Zhedong's mountains and sea are secluded and obstructive; it can be taken by stratagem but is hard to seize by force.
translations.idiomatic: Xiahou Zi said, "Zhedong's rugged coast and hills favor stratagem over brute force.

sentences.zh: 西班中無可語者。

translations.literal: Among the western-shift officials there is no one worth speaking of.
translations.idiomatic: None of the western-shift ministers are equal to the task.

sentences.zh: 前安南都護王式，雖儒家子，在安南威服華夷，名聞遠近，可任也。」

translations.literal: The former Protector-General of Annan, Wang Shi, though a Confucian by upbringing, in Annan awed both Chinese and barbarians; his fame reaches far and near. He can be entrusted with the post."
translations.idiomatic: Former Annan protector-general Wang Shi, though raised as a scholar, subdued Chinese and foreign peoples alike in the south; his reputation is known far and wide. He is the man for this job."

sentences.zh: 諸相皆以為然。

translations.literal: All the chief ministers agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers all agreed.

sentences.zh: 遂以式為浙東觀察使，征祗德為賓客。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shi was appointed military governor of Zhedong, and Qide was recalled as a court guest.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was appointed governor of Zhedong, and Qide was recalled to serve as a court guest.

sentences.zh: 三月，辛亥朔，式入對，上問以討賊方略。

translations.literal: Third month, first day of the month xinhai, Shi entered audience; the emperor asked him for his strategy to suppress the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: On the first xinhai day of the third month, Shi had an audience with the emperor, who asked how he would defeat the rebels.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「但得兵，賊必可破。」

translations.literal: He replied: "If I am given troops, the rebels can certainly be broken."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Give me troops, and the rebels will surely be broken."

sentences.zh: 有宦官侍側，曰：「發兵，所費甚大。」

translations.literal: A eunuch attending at his side said: "Dispatching troops costs a great deal."
translations.idiomatic: A eunuch at the emperor's side said, "Raising an army is terribly expensive."

sentences.zh: 式曰：「臣為國家惜費則不然。

translations.literal: Shi said: "Your servant is not one to be sparing of expense on the state's behalf in that sense.
translations.idiomatic: Shi replied, "I am not urging thrift in that narrow sense.

sentences.zh: 兵多賊速破，其費省矣。

translations.literal: With many troops the rebels are quickly broken, and the expense is thereby reduced.
translations.idiomatic: A large force will crush the rebels quickly and cost less in the end.

sentences.zh: 若兵少不能勝賊，延引歲月，賊勢益張，則江、淮群盜將蜂起應之。

translations.literal: If the troops are few and cannot overcome the rebels, and months drag on while rebel strength grows, then bandits along the Yangzi and Huai will rise like bees to join them.
translations.idiomatic: If we send too few men and the campaign drags on, rebel power will swell and bandits along the Yangzi and Huai will rise to join them.

sentences.zh: 國家用度盡仰江、淮，若阻絕不通，則上自九廟，下及十軍，皆無以供給，其費豈可勝計哉！」

translations.literal: The state's expenditures all depend on the Yangzi and Huai; if transport is cut off, then from the imperial ancestral temples above to the ten armies below, none will have supplies. How can such a cost be calculated!"
translations.idiomatic: The empire's revenue depends entirely on the Yangzi and Huai. Cut those routes, and from the ancestral temples to every army in the field, nothing will be supplied. That cost cannot even be reckoned!"

sentences.zh: 上顧宦官曰：「當與之兵。」

translations.literal: The emperor turned to the eunuch and said: "He shall be given troops."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to the eunuch and said, "Give him the troops he needs."

sentences.zh: 乃詔發忠武、義成、淮南等諸道兵授之。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued to mobilize troops from the Zhongwu, Yicheng, Huainan, and other circuits and place them under his command.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered troops from Zhongwu, Yicheng, Huainan, and other circuits placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 裘甫分兵掠衢、婺州。

translations.literal: Qiu Fu divided his forces to plunder Qu and Wu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Fu sent detachments to raid Qu and Wu prefectures.

sentences.zh: 婺州押牙房郅、散將樓曾、衢州十將方景深將兵拒險，賊不得入。

translations.literal: Wu Prefecture's yamen guard Fang Zhi, the irregular commander Lou Zeng, and Quzhou's tenth-rank officer Fang Jingshen led troops to hold the defiles, and the rebels could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Zhi of Wu, irregular commander Lou Zeng, and Quzhou officer Fang Jingshen held the passes, and the rebels could not break through.

sentences.zh: 又分兵掠明州，明州之民相與謀曰：「賊若入城，妻子皆為菹醢，況貨財，能保之乎！」

translations.literal: He again sent troops to plunder Ming Prefecture. The people of Ming conferred among themselves and said: "If the rebels enter the city, wives and children will all be minced meat—how much less can goods and wealth be preserved!"
translations.idiomatic: He sent another force against Ming Prefecture. The people there said to one another, "If the rebels take the city, our families will be butchered—what hope is there for our goods?"

sentences.zh: 乃自相帥出財募勇士，治器械，樹柵，浚溝，斷橋，為固守之備。

translations.literal: Thereupon they took the lead among themselves, contributed funds to recruit brave men, prepared weapons, erected palisades, dug ditches, and destroyed bridges to make preparations for a stubborn defense.
translations.idiomatic: They pooled their wealth, recruited fighters, forged arms, built palisades, dug ditches, and destroyed bridges to prepare a stubborn defense.

sentences.zh: 賊又遣兵掠台州，破唐興。

translations.literal: The rebels again sent troops to plunder Taizhou and overran Tangxing.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels raided Taizhou as well and overran Tangxing.

sentences.zh: 己巳，甫自將萬餘人掠上虞，焚之。

translations.literal: On the day jisi, Fu personally led more than ten thousand men to plunder Shangyu and burned it.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Fu personally led more than ten thousand men against Shangyu and burned the town.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，入余姚，殺丞、尉。

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, he entered Yuyao and killed the assistant magistrate and the district captain.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, he entered Yuyao and killed the assistant magistrate and district captain.

sentences.zh: 東破慈溪，入奉化，抵寧海，殺其令而據之，分兵圍象山。

translations.literal: Eastward he broke Cixi, entered Fenghua, reached Ninghai, killed its magistrate and occupied it, and sent a detachment to besiege Xiangshan.
translations.idiomatic: He smashed Cixi to the east, took Fenghua, reached Ninghai, killed the magistrate and held the town, and sent troops to besiege Xiangshan.

sentences.zh: 所過俘其少壯，餘老弱者蹂踐殺之。

translations.literal: Wherever he passed he took the young and strong captive; the rest, old and weak, he trampled and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he marched he took the able-bodied captive and trampled or killed the old and weak.

sentences.zh: 及王式除書下，浙東人心稍安。

translations.literal: When Wang Shi's appointment decree was issued, hearts in Zhedong were somewhat reassured.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shi's appointment was announced, the people of Zhedong took heart.

sentences.zh: 裘甫方與其徒飲酒，聞之不樂。

translations.literal: Qiu Fu was just drinking with his followers; on hearing the news he was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Fu was drinking with his men when he heard the news and turned gloomy.

sentences.zh: 劉暀歎曰：「有如此之眾，而策畫未定，良可惜也！

translations.literal: Liu Chang sighed and said: "With a host like this, yet no plan settled—how truly regrettable!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang sighed, "With a force this large and still no settled plan—it is a waste!

sentences.zh: 今朝廷遣王中丞將兵來，聞其人智勇無敵，不四十日必至。

translations.literal: Now the court has sent Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang with troops; I hear that man's wisdom and courage are unmatched, and he will arrive within forty days at the latest.
translations.idiomatic: The court has sent Vice Censor Wang Shi with an army. They say he is unrivaled in wit and valor and will be here within forty days.

sentences.zh: 兵馬使宜急引兵取越州，憑城郭，據府庫，遣兵五千守西陵，循浙江築壘以拒之。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief should hurry to lead troops to seize Yue Prefecture, rely on its walls, hold the government treasury, send five thousand men to guard Xiling, and build fortifications along the Zhe River to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Commander, march at once on Yue Prefecture, hold its walls and treasury, post five thousand men at Xiling, and build fortifications along the Zhe River to block him.

sentences.zh: 大集舟艦，得間，則長驅進取浙西，過大江，掠揚州貨財以自實。

translations.literal: Amass ships in great numbers; when an opening appears, drive straight west to seize Zhexi, cross the great river, and plunder Yangzhou's goods and wealth to strengthen yourselves.
translations.idiomatic: Gather a fleet; when the moment comes, strike west into Zhexi, cross the Yangzi, and loot Yangzhou to fill your coffers.

sentences.zh: 還，修石頭城而守之，宣歙、江西必有響應者。

translations.literal: Return, repair Stone City and hold it; Xuan-She and Jiangxi will surely have men who answer your call.
translations.idiomatic: Then fall back, repair Stone City, and hold it—Xuan-She and Jiangxi will rise to join you.

sentences.zh: 遣劉從簡以萬人循海而南，襲取福建。

translations.literal: Send Liu Congjian with ten thousand men along the coast southward to strike and seize Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Send Liu Congjian with ten thousand men down the coast to seize Fujian.

sentences.zh: 如此，則國家貢賦之地盡入於我矣。

translations.literal: Thus the regions from which the state draws its tribute and taxes will all fall into our hands.
translations.idiomatic: Do this, and the empire's richest tribute lands will be ours.

sentences.zh: 但恐子孫不能守耳，終吾身保無憂也。」

translations.literal: I only fear later generations may not be able to hold them; for the rest of my own life we can be secure without worry."
translations.idiomatic: Only our descendants may fail to hold what we win—in your own lifetime, you need not worry."

sentences.zh: 甫曰：「醉矣，明日議之！」

translations.literal: Fu said: "I am drunk; we will discuss it tomorrow!"
translations.idiomatic: Fu said, "I am drunk—we will talk tomorrow!

sentences.zh: 暀以甫不用其言，怒，陽醉而出。

translations.literal: Chang, because Fu would not adopt his counsel, was angry and left in feigned drunkenness.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, angry that Fu ignored him, pretended to be drunk and stalked out.

sentences.zh: 有進士王輅在賊中，賊客之，輅說甫曰：「如劉副使之謀，乃孫權所為也。

translations.literal: A jinshi named Wang Lu was among the rebels; they treated him as an honored guest. Lu urged Fu: "Deputy Commander Liu's plan is what Sun Quan did.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi named Wang Lu was with the rebels and was treated as an honored guest. He told Fu, "Liu's plan is Sun Quan's old strategy.

sentences.zh: 彼乘天下大亂，故能據有江東；

translations.literal: He rode the great disorder under heaven and therefore was able to hold the lands east of the Yangzi;
translations.idiomatic: Sun seized the moment when the empire was in chaos and held the lower Yangzi;

sentences.zh: 今中國無事，此功未易成也。

translations.literal: now the Central Realm is untroubled, and this achievement will not be easy to accomplish.
translations.idiomatic: but the realm is at peace now, and such a feat will not be easy.

sentences.zh: 不如擁眾據險自守，陸耕海漁，急則逃入海島，此萬全策也。」

translations.literal: Better to gather your host, hold the defiles, and defend yourselves—farm on land, fish at sea; in urgency flee to the sea islands. This is the plan of perfect safety."
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold the hills with your host, farm the land and fish the sea, and flee to the islands if pressed—that is the sure plan.

sentences.zh: 甫畏式，猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Fu feared Wang Shi and hesitated, unable to decide.
translations.idiomatic: Fu feared Wang Shi and could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，式行至柿口，義成軍不整，式欲斬其將，久乃釋之，自是軍所過若無人。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Shi reached Shikou. The Yicheng army was not in order; Shi wished to behead its commander but after a long while released him. From then on wherever the army passed it was as if no one were there.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Shi reached Shikou. The Yicheng troops were disorderly; Shi nearly executed their commander but relented after a long delay. From then on, the army marched through the land in utter silence.

sentences.zh: 至西陵，裘甫遣使請降。

translations.literal: When he reached Xiling, Qiu Fu sent envoys to request surrender.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiling, Qiu Fu sent envoys offering surrender.

sentences.zh: 式曰：「是必無降心，直欲窺吾所為，且欲使吾驕怠耳。」

translations.literal: Shi said: "They certainly have no mind to surrender; they only wish to spy on what we are doing and moreover to make us proud and slack."
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "They have no intention of surrendering. They want to spy on us and lull us into arrogance and slackness.

sentences.zh: 乃謂使者曰：「甫面縛以來，當免而死。」

translations.literal: He then told the envoys: "If Fu comes with his face bound, he shall be spared and live."
translations.idiomatic: He told the envoys, "If Fu comes with his hands bound, he may live.

sentences.zh: 乙未，式入越州，既交政，為鄭祗德置酒，曰：「式主軍政，不可以飲，監軍但與眾賓盡醉。」

translations.literal: On the day yiwei, Shi entered Yue Prefecture. After handing over administration, he held a banquet for Zheng Qide and said: "Shi directs military affairs and may not drink; the army supervisor and all the guests should drink their fill."
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Shi entered Yue Prefecture. After taking office he gave a banquet for Zheng Qide and said, "I command the campaign and cannot drink, but the army supervisor and every guest should drink their fill.

sentences.zh: 迨夜，繼以燭，曰：「式在此，賊安能妨人樂飲！」

translations.literal: When night came he had candles brought forth and said: "With Shi here, how can rebels keep people from drinking in pleasure!"
translations.idiomatic: When night fell he ordered more lamps and said, "While I am here, how can rebels stop anyone from enjoying a feast?

sentences.zh: 丙申，餞祗德於遠郊，復樂飲而歸。

translations.literal: On the day bingshen he gave Qide a farewell feast in the distant suburbs, then returned in merry drinking.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen he gave Qide a farewell feast in the outer suburbs, then returned still drinking in high spirits.

sentences.zh: 於是始修軍令，告饋餉不足者息矣，稱疾臥家者起矣，先求遷職者默矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he first restored military regulations: those who complained that rations were insufficient fell silent; those who claimed illness and lay at home rose; those who had first sought promotion in rank grew quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Then he enforced military discipline. Complaints about short rations ceased, men who had feigned illness got up, and those who had demanded promotions fell silent.

sentences.zh: 賊別帥洪師簡、許會能帥所部降。

translations.literal: The rebel sub-chiefs Hong Shijian and Xu Huineng led their followers to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel lieutenants Hong Shijian and Xu Huineng surrendered with their bands.

sentences.zh: 式曰：「汝降是也，當立效以自異。」

translations.literal: Shi said: "Your surrender is acceptable, but you must establish merit to distinguish yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "Surrender is well enough, but you must earn your keep.

sentences.zh: 使帥其徒為前鋒，與賊戰有功，乃奏以官。

translations.literal: He had them lead their followers as vanguard; when they fought the rebels with merit, he then memorialized for their official appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He made them lead their men as vanguard; only after they fought well against the rebels did he recommend them for office.

sentences.zh: 先是，賊諜入越州，軍吏匿而飲食之。

translations.literal: Earlier, rebel spies had entered Yue Prefecture; army officers concealed them and gave them food and drink.
translations.idiomatic: Before this, rebel spies had entered Yue Prefecture, and army officers had hidden and fed them.

sentences.zh: 文武將吏往往潛與賊通，求城破之日免死及全妻子。

translations.literal: Civil and military officers often secretly communicated with the rebels, seeking on the day the city fell to be spared death and to preserve their wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officers had often secretly dealt with the rebels, hoping to save their lives and families when the city fell.

sentences.zh: 或詐引賊將來降，實窺虛實。

translations.literal: Some feigned to bring rebel commanders to surrender while in fact spying out strengths and weaknesses.
translations.idiomatic: Some pretended to bring rebel leaders in to surrender while actually scouting the city's defenses.

sentences.zh: 城中密謀屏語，賊皆知之。

translations.literal: Secret plots and whispered words within the city were all known to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Every whispered plot inside the city reached the rebels.

sentences.zh: 式陰察知，悉捕索，斬之。

translations.literal: Shi secretly investigated and learned of it, seized them all, and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi uncovered the leaks, arrested the culprits, and executed them.

sentences.zh: 刑將吏尤橫猾者，嚴門禁，無驗者不得出入，警夜周密，賊始不知我所為矣。

translations.literal: He punished the most overbearing and cunning officers, tightened the gate regulations so that none without credentials could enter or leave, and made night watches thorough; only then did the rebels cease to know what we were doing.
translations.idiomatic: He punished the worst offenders among the officers, tightened the gates so only authorized men could pass, and posted rigorous night watches—only then did the rebels lose sight of his plans.

sentences.zh: 式命諸縣開倉廩以賑貧乏，或曰：「賊未滅，軍食方急，不可散也。」

translations.literal: Shi ordered the counties to open their granaries to relieve the poor and needy. Someone said: "The rebels are not yet destroyed, and army provisions are urgently needed; grain must not be dispersed."
translations.idiomatic: Shi ordered the counties to open their granaries to feed the poor. Someone objected, "The rebels are not beaten yet and army grain is scarce—we cannot give it away.

sentences.zh: 式曰：「非汝所知。」

translations.literal: Shi said: "That is not for you to understand."
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "That is not for you to understand.

sentences.zh: 官軍少騎卒，式曰：「吐蕃、回鶻比配江、淮者，其人習險阻，便鞍馬，可用也。」

translations.literal: The government army had few cavalry. Shi said: "Among the Tibetans and Uyghurs assigned in rotation to the Yangzi and Huai regions, the men are accustomed to rugged terrain and skilled with saddle and horse; they can be used."
translations.idiomatic: The government army lacked cavalry. Shi said, "The Tibetan and Uyghur troops stationed in rotation along the Yangzi and Huai know rough country and are skilled horsemen—they will serve.

sentences.zh: 舉籍府中，得驍健者百餘人。

translations.literal: He reviewed the registers in the prefectural compound and obtained more than a hundred stalwart men.
translations.idiomatic: He searched the prefectural registers and found more than a hundred able men.

sentences.zh: 虜久羈旅，所部遇之無狀，困餒甚。

translations.literal: The barbarians had long been detained far from home; those under whom they served treated them shamefully, and they were greatly afflicted with hunger and exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: These men had been held far from home for years, ill-treated by their overseers, and were starving.

sentences.zh: 式既犒飲，又賙其父母妻子，皆泣拜歡呼，願效死，悉以為騎卒，使騎將石宗本將之。

translations.literal: After Shi feasted and rewarded them and also gave relief to their parents, wives, and children, they all wept, bowed, and shouted for joy, willing to die in his service; he made them all cavalry and had the cavalry commander Shi Zongben lead them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi feasted them, gave gifts to their families, and they wept and shouted their willingness to die for him. He enrolled them all as cavalry under Shi Zongben.

sentences.zh: 凡在管內者，皆視此籍之，又奏得龍陂監馬二百匹，於是騎兵足矣。

translations.literal: All such men within his jurisdiction were enrolled in the same way; he also memorialized for two hundred horses from Longpo Stud and thereby had cavalry in sufficient number.
translations.idiomatic: He enrolled every able man in the circuit the same way, secured two hundred horses from Longpo Stud, and at last had enough cavalry.

sentences.zh: 或請為烽燧以詗賊遠近眾寡，式笑而不應。

translations.literal: Some asked to build beacon towers to reconnoiter the rebels' distance, nearness, and numbers; Shi smiled and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Some proposed beacon towers to track rebel movements; Shi only smiled and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 選懦卒，使乘健馬，少與之兵，以為候騎。

translations.literal: He chose cowardly soldiers, had them ride strong horses, gave them few troops, and made them scouting horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: He picked the timidest soldiers, mounted them on the best horses with only a few men each, and sent them out as scouts.

sentences.zh: 眾怪之，不敢問。

translations.literal: The troops thought it strange but dared not ask.
translations.idiomatic: The men were baffled but dared not question him.

sentences.zh: 於是閱諸營見卒及土糰子弟，得四千人，使導軍分路討賊。

translations.literal: Thereupon he reviewed the troops on hand in the camps and the local militia youths, obtained four thousand men, and had them guide the army on separate routes to attack the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: He then mustered garrison troops and local militia youths, raised four thousand guides, and sent the army against the rebels on several routes.

sentences.zh: 府下無守兵，更籍土團千人以補之。

translations.literal: Under the prefectural seat there were no garrison troops; he again enrolled a thousand local militia to fill the gap.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural seat had no garrison, so he enrolled another thousand militiamen to guard it.

sentences.zh: 乃命宣歙將白琮、浙西將凌茂貞帥本軍，北來將韓宗政等帥土團，合千人；

translations.literal: He then ordered the Xuan-She commander Bai Cong and the Zhexi commander Ling Maozhen to lead their own armies, and the northern commander Han Zongzheng and others to lead the local militia—a combined force of a thousand men;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Xuan-She commander Bai Cong and Zhexi commander Ling Maozhen with their own troops, and northern commander Han Zongzheng with the militia—a thousand men in all;

sentences.zh: 石宗本帥騎兵為前鋒，自上虞趨奉化，解像山之圍，號東路軍。

translations.literal: Shi Zongben led the cavalry as vanguard, hastened from Shangyu toward Fenghua, relieved the siege of Xiangshan, and this force was styled the Eastern Route Army.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zongben led the cavalry from Shangyu toward Fenghua, lifted the siege of Xiangshan, and this column was called the Eastern Route Army.

sentences.zh: 又以義成將白宗建、忠武將游君楚、淮南將萬璘帥本軍與台州唐興軍合，號南路軍。

translations.literal: He also had the Yicheng commander Bai Zongjian, the Zhongwu commander You Junchu, and the Huainan commander Wan Lin lead their own armies to join the Tangxing army of Taizhou; this was styled the Southern Route Army.
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng commander Bai Zongjian, Zhongwu commander You Junchu, and Huainan commander Wan Lin led their troops to join the Tangxing garrison of Taizhou in the Southern Route Army.

sentences.zh: 令之曰：「毋爭險易，毋焚廬舍，毋殺平民以增首級！

translations.literal: He charged them: "Do not dispute over difficult or easy ground, do not burn dwellings, do not kill civilians to pad your head counts!
translations.idiomatic: He ordered them, "Do not quarrel over easy or hard assignments, do not burn homes, and do not kill civilians to pad your body counts!

sentences.zh: 平民脅從者，募降之。

translations.literal: As for commoners who had been coerced to follow, he recruited them to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: For civilians who had been forced to join the rebels, he offered terms to accept their surrender.

sentences.zh: 得賊金帛，官無所問。

translations.literal: If they had obtained gold and silk from the rebels, the authorities would not inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who had taken gold or silk from the rebels would not be questioned by the authorities.

sentences.zh: 俘獲者，皆越人也，釋之。」

translations.literal: Those captured were all people of Yue; he released them."
translations.idiomatic: All captives were natives of the region, and he set them free."

sentences.zh: 癸卯，南路軍拔賊沃州寨，甲辰，拔新昌寨，破賊將毛應天，進抵唐興。

translations.literal: On the day guimao, the Southern Route Army captured the rebel stronghold at Wo Prefecture; on the day jiachen it captured the Xinchang stronghold, defeated the rebel general Mao Yingtian, and advanced to Tangxing.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the Southern Route Army took the rebel stronghold at Wo Prefecture; on jiachen it took Xinchang, defeated rebel general Mao Yingtian, and pushed on to Tangxing.

sentences.zh: 白敏中三表辭位，上不許。

translations.literal: Bai Minzhong thrice submitted memorials resigning his office; the emperor did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Minzhong submitted three memorials asking to resign, but the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 右補闕王譜上疏，以為：「陛下致理之初，乃宰相盡心之日，不可暫闕。

translations.literal: Right Remonstrance Wang Pu submitted a memorial, stating: "At the beginning of Your Majesty's pursuit of good order, this is the time when the chief minister should give his full devotion—it must not be vacant even briefly.
translations.idiomatic: Right Remonstrance Wang Pu submitted a memorial arguing that at the start of Your Majesty's reign, when the chief minister should be giving his utmost, the post must not stand empty even for a moment.

sentences.zh: 敏中自正月臥疾，今四月矣，陛下雖與他相坐語，未嘗三刻，天下之事，陛下嘗暇與之講論乎！

translations.literal: Minzhong has been bedridden since the first month—now it is the fourth month. Though Your Majesty sits and speaks with the other ministers, it has never reached three quarters of an hour. Have you ever had leisure to discuss the affairs of the empire with him?
translations.idiomatic: Minzhong has been ill in bed since the first month, and it is now the fourth. Though Your Majesty has sat with the other ministers, you have never spoken with him for as long as three quarters of an hour. When have you found time to discuss the affairs of the realm with him?

sentences.zh: 願聽敏中罷去，延訪碩德，以資聰明。」

translations.literal: I beg that Minzhong be allowed to retire, and that eminent worthies be summoned to assist Your Majesty's clear judgment."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Minzhong be permitted to step down and that men of great virtue be sought out to aid Your Majesty's wisdom.

sentences.zh: 己酉，貶譜為陽翟令。

translations.literal: On the day jiyou, Pu was demoted to magistrate of Yangdi.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Pu was demoted to magistrate of Yangdi.

sentences.zh: 譜，珪之六世孫也。

translations.literal: Pu was the sixth-generation descendant of Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was a sixth-generation descendant of Wang Gui.

sentences.zh: 五月，庚戌朔，給事中鄭公輿封還貶譜敕書。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on the gengxu new moon, Supervising Secretary Zheng Gongyu returned sealed the edict demoting Pu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the first day of the month, gengxu, Supervising Secretary Zheng Gongyu sealed and returned the edict demoting Pu.

sentences.zh: 上令宰相議之，宰相以為譜侵敏中，竟貶之。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the chief ministers to discuss it; the chief ministers held that Pu had affronted Minzhong, and in the end demoted him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the chief ministers to deliberate; they decided Pu had insulted Minzhong, and he was demoted after all.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，浙東東路軍破賊將孫馬騎於寧海。

translations.literal: On the day xinhai, the Eastern Zhedong Route Army defeated the rebel general Sun Maqi at Ninghai.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the Eastern Zhedong Route Army defeated rebel general Sun Maqi at Ninghai.

sentences.zh: 戊午，南路軍大破賊將劉暀、毛應天於唐興南谷，斬應天。

translations.literal: On the day wuwu, the Southern Route Army heavily defeated the rebel generals Liu Chang and Mao Yingtian at Tangxing's South Valley; Yingtian was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu the Southern Route Army routed rebel generals Liu Chang and Mao Yingtian in Tangxing's South Valley and beheaded Yingtian.

sentences.zh: 先是，王式以兵少，奏更發忠武、義成軍及請昭義軍，詔從之。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Wang Shi's forces were few, he memorialized requesting additional dispatch of the Zhongwu and Yicheng armies and asking for the Zhaoyi army; an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, finding his forces too few, Wang Shi had memorialized for reinforcements from the Zhongwu and Yicheng armies and for the Zhaoyi army as well; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 三道兵至越州，式命忠武將張茵將三百人屯唐興，斷賊南出之道；

translations.literal: Troops from the three routes reached Yue Prefecture. Shi ordered the Zhongwu commander Zhang Yin to lead three hundred men to garrison Tangxing and cut off the rebels' route south;
translations.idiomatic: When troops from all three routes reached Yue Prefecture, Shi ordered Zhongwu commander Zhang Yin with three hundred men to hold Tangxing and block the rebels' escape to the south;

sentences.zh: 義成將高羅銳將三百人，益以台州土軍，逕趨寧海，攻賊巢穴；

translations.literal: the Yicheng commander Gao Luorui to lead three hundred men, augmented by Taizhou local militia, to press directly toward Ninghai and attack the rebel nest;
translations.idiomatic: Yicheng commander Gao Luorui with three hundred men, reinforced by Taizhou militia, to strike straight for Ninghai and hit the rebel stronghold;

sentences.zh: 昭義將□夾跌戣將四百人，益東路軍，斷賊入明州之道。

translations.literal: and the Zhaoyi commander Qibi Die Wei (name partly lost in manuscript) to lead four hundred men, augmented by the Eastern Route army, to cut off the rebels' route into Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: and Zhaoyi commander Qibi Die Wei, with four hundred men, joined to the Eastern Route army, to seal the rebels' path into Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 庚申，南路軍大破賊於海游鎮，賊入甬溪洞。

translations.literal: On the day gengshen, the Southern Route Army heavily defeated the rebels at Haiyou town; the rebels entered Yongxi cave.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen the Southern Route Army routed the rebels at Haiyou, driving them into Yongxi cave.

sentences.zh: 戊辰，官軍屯於洞口，賊出洞戰，又破之。

translations.literal: On the day wuchen, the government troops encamped at the cave mouth; the rebels came out to fight and were defeated again.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen government troops camped at the cave mouth; the rebels sallied out and were beaten once more.

sentences.zh: 己巳，高羅銳襲賊別帥劉平天寨，破之。

translations.literal: On the day jisi, Gao Luorui raided the rebel sub-commander Liu Pingtian's stronghold and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi Gao Luorui stormed rebel lieutenant Liu Pingtian's camp and took it.

sentences.zh: 自是諸軍與賊十九戰，賊連敗。

translations.literal: From then on the various armies fought the rebels nineteen battles, and the rebels suffered continuous defeats.
translations.idiomatic: From that point the allied armies fought nineteen engagements with the rebels, who lost again and again.

sentences.zh: 劉暀謂裘甫曰：「向從吾謀入趙州，寧有此困邪！」

translations.literal: Liu Chang said to Qiu Fu: "If you had followed my plan to enter Zhao Prefecture, would we be in such straits!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chang told Qiu Fu, "If you had taken my advice and marched into Zhao Prefecture, would we be in this fix?

sentences.zh: 王輅等進士數人在賊中，皆衣綠，暀悉斬之，曰：「亂我謀者，此青蟲也！」

translations.literal: Several jinshi degree holders such as Wang Luo were among the rebels, all wearing green robes; Chang beheaded them all, saying, "Those who ruin my plans are these green worms!"
translations.idiomatic: Several jinshi such as Wang Luo were with the rebels, all in green robes. Chang executed them all, saying, "These green worms are the ones who wrecked my plans!

sentences.zh: 高羅銳克寧海，收其逃散之民，得七千餘人。

translations.literal: Gao Luorui took Ninghai and gathered its scattered populace, obtaining more than seven thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Luorui captured Ninghai and rounded up more than seven thousand of its scattered inhabitants.

sentences.zh: 王式曰：「賊窘且饑，必逃入海，入海則歲月間未可擒也。」

translations.literal: Wang Shi said: "The rebels are cornered and hungry; they are sure to flee into the sea. Once at sea, they cannot be captured within months."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shi said, "The rebels are desperate and starving. They will surely flee to sea, and once they do we may not catch them for months.

sentences.zh: 命羅銳軍海口以拒之。

translations.literal: He ordered Luorui's army to hold the harbor mouth to block them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Luorui's force to hold the harbor mouth and block their escape.

sentences.zh: 又命望海鎮將雲思益、浙西將王克容將水軍巡海澨。

translations.literal: He also ordered the Wanghaizhen commander Yun Siyi and the Zhexi commander Wang Kerong to lead naval forces to patrol the coastal shallows.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Wanghaizhen commander Yun Siyi and Zhexi commander Wang Kerong to patrol the coast with the fleet.

sentences.zh: 思益等遇賊將劉從簡於寧海東，賊不虞水軍遽至，皆棄船走山谷，得其船十七，盡焚之。

translations.literal: Siyi and the others encountered the rebel general Liu Congjian east of Ninghai; the rebels did not expect the naval force to arrive so suddenly—all abandoned their boats and fled into mountain valleys. Seventeen boats were captured and all burned.
translations.idiomatic: East of Ninghai, Siyi and his men met rebel general Liu Congjian. Caught off guard by the sudden arrival of the fleet, the rebels abandoned their boats and fled into the hills. Seventeen vessels were seized and burned.

sentences.zh: 式曰：「賊無所逃矣，惟黃罕嶺可入剡，恨無兵以守之。

translations.literal: Shi said: "The rebels have nowhere left to flee. Only Huanghan Ridge leads into Shan; I regret we have no troops to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "The rebels have nowhere left to run. Only Huanghan Ridge offers a way into Shan, and I regret we have no force to guard it.

sentences.zh: 雖然，亦成擒矣！」

translations.literal: Even so, their capture is assured!"
translations.idiomatic: Even so, we will take them!

sentences.zh: 裘甫既失寧海，乃帥其徒屯南陳館下，眾尚萬餘人。

translations.literal: Qiu Fu, having lost Ninghai, then led his band to encamp below Nanchen Station; his followers still numbered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost Ninghai, Qiu Fu led his followers to camp below Nanchen Station, where he still had more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 辛未，東路軍破賊將孫馬騎於上□村，賊將王皋懼，請降。

translations.literal: On the day xinwei, the Eastern Route Army defeated the rebel general Sun Maqi at Shang□ Village; the rebel general Wang Gao, in fear, requested to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the Eastern Route Army defeated rebel general Sun Maqi at Shang□ Village; rebel general Wang Gao, terrified, offered to surrender.

sentences.zh: 壬申，右拾遺內供奉薛調上言，以為：「兵興以來，賦斂無度，所在群盜，半是逃戶，固須翦滅，亦可閔傷。

translations.literal: On the day renshen, Right Palace Remonstrator-in-Ordinary Xue Tiao submitted a statement, holding that: "Since troops were raised, levies have been boundless; everywhere bandits are half fugitive households. They must be cut down, yet pity is also owed.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Right Palace Remonstrator-in-Ordinary Xue Tiao submitted a memorial arguing that since the war began, taxation had run without limit and many local bandits were fugitive taxpayers. They had to be suppressed, he said, but they also deserved compassion.

sentences.zh: 望敕州縣稅外毋得科率，仍敕長吏嚴加糾察。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will order that prefectures and counties impose no exactions beyond regular taxes, and command local chiefs to investigate strictly."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that prefectures and counties be forbidden to levy anything beyond regular taxes, and that local officials be ordered to investigate abuses strictly.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 袁王紳薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Yuan Wang Shen died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yuan Wang Shen died.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，浙東東路軍大破裘甫於南陳館，斬首數千級，賊委棄繒帛盈路，以緩追者，□夾跌戣令士卒：「敢顧者斬！」

translations.literal: On the day wuyin, the Eastern Zhedong Route Army heavily defeated Qiu Fu at Nanchen Station, cutting off several thousand heads. The rebels abandoned silk and brocade to fill the road and slow pursuit. Qibi Die Wei ordered the soldiers: "Whoever looks back shall be beheaded!"
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the Eastern Zhedong Route Army routed Qiu Fu at Nanchen Station, taking several thousand heads. The rebels left silk and brocade strewn along the road to slow pursuit. Qibi Die Wei ordered his men, "Anyone who looks back will be executed!

sentences.zh: 毋敢犯者。

translations.literal: None dared violate this.
translations.idiomatic: No one dared disobey.

sentences.zh: 賊果自黃罕嶺遁去，六月，甲申，復入剡。

translations.literal: The rebels indeed escaped through Huanghan Ridge; in the sixth month, on the day jiashen, they entered Shan again.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels did escape through Huanghan Ridge, and in the sixth month, on jiashen, they re-entered Shan.

sentences.zh: 諸軍失甫，不知所在，義成將張茵在唐興獲俘，將苦之，俘曰：「賊入剡矣。

translations.literal: The armies lost track of Fu and did not know where he was. The Yicheng commander Zhang Yin at Tangxing captured a prisoner and was about to torture him; the prisoner said, "The rebels have entered Shan.
translations.idiomatic: The armies lost Qiu Fu and had no idea where he was. At Tangxing, Yicheng commander Zhang Yin captured a prisoner and was about to torture him when the man said, "The rebels have gone into Shan.

sentences.zh: 苟捨我，我請為軍導。」

translations.literal: If you spare me, I will guide the army."
translations.idiomatic: Spare me, and I will lead your army.

sentences.zh: 從之，茵後甫一日至剡，壁其東南，府中聞甫入剡，復大恐，王式曰：「賊來就擒耳！」

translations.literal: Yin complied; he reached Shan one day after Fu and fortified the southeast. When the prefectural seat heard Fu had entered Shan, great fear arose again. Wang Shi said, "The rebels come to be captured!"
translations.idiomatic: Yin agreed. He reached Shan a day after Fu and fortified the southeast. When the prefectural seat heard Fu was in Shan, panic spread again. Wang Shi said, "The rebels are delivering themselves into our hands!

sentences.zh: 命趣東、南兩路軍會於剡，辛卯，圍之，賊城守甚堅，攻之，不能拔，諸將議絕溪水以渴之，賊知之，乃出戰。

translations.literal: He ordered the Eastern and Southern route armies to converge at Shan. On the day xinmao they invested it. The rebels held the city very firmly; assault could not take it. The generals discussed cutting off the stream to thirst them out; the rebels learned of this and came out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Eastern and Southern route armies to converge on Shan. On xinmao they besieged the city, but the rebels held it stubbornly and could not be stormed. When the generals proposed cutting off the stream to starve them of water, the rebels learned of the plan and sallied out to fight.

sentences.zh: 三日，凡八十三戰，賊雖敗，官軍亦疲。

translations.literal: In three days they fought eighty-three battles; though the rebels lost, the government troops were also exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Over three days they fought eighty-three engagements. The rebels kept losing, but the government army was worn out too.

sentences.zh: 賊請降，諸將出以白式，式曰：「賊欲少休耳，益謹備之，功垂成矣。」

translations.literal: The rebels requested surrender; the generals went out to report to Shi. Shi said, "The rebels only want a brief rest. Guard all the more strictly—victory is at hand."
translations.idiomatic: The rebels asked to surrender. When the generals reported this to Shi, he said, "They only want a breather. Tighten the defenses—victory is almost ours.

sentences.zh: 賊果復出，又三戰。

translations.literal: The rebels indeed came out again and fought three more battles.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels did sally out again, and three more battles followed.

sentences.zh: 庚子夜，裘甫、劉□往、劉慶從百餘人出降，遙與諸將語，離城數十步，官軍疾趨，斷其後，遂擒之，壬寅，甫等至越州，式腰斬暀、慶等二十餘人，械甫送京師。

translations.literal: On the night of gengzi, Qiu Fu, Liu Wang (name partly lost in manuscript), Liu Qingcong, and more than a hundred others came out to surrender. From afar they spoke with the generals; when several tens of paces from the city, government troops rushed forward, cut off their rear, and captured them. On the day renyin, Fu and the others reached Yue Prefecture; Shi had Chang, Qing, and more than twenty others executed at the waist and sent Fu in fetters to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of gengzi, Qiu Fu, Liu Wang, Liu Qingcong, and more than a hundred followers came out to surrender. They spoke with the generals from a distance, but when they were several dozen paces from the city wall, government troops rushed in and cut off their retreat. On renyin, Fu and the others reached Yue Prefecture. Shi had Chang, Qing, and more than twenty others executed by waist-slicing and sent Fu to the capital in chains.

sentences.zh: 剡城猶未下，諸將已擒甫，不復設備。

translations.literal: Shan city had still not fallen; the generals, having captured Fu, no longer maintained their defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Shan city had not yet fallen, but once the generals had captured Fu they relaxed their guard.

sentences.zh: 劉從簡帥壯士五百突圍走，諸將追至大蘭山，從簡據險自守。

translations.literal: Liu Congjian led five hundred stalwart men to break out and flee; the generals pursued to Mount Dalán, and Congjian held the defensible ground.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Congjian broke out with five hundred picked men. The generals pursued him to Mount Dalán, where he held the high ground.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丁巳，諸將共攻克之。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on the day dingsi, the generals jointly stormed and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on dingsi, the generals jointly stormed and captured the position.

sentences.zh: 台州刺史李師望募賊相捕斬之以自贖，所降數百人，得從簡首，獻之。

translations.literal: Taizhou prefect Li Shiwang recruited rebels to capture and behead one another for redemption; several hundred who surrendered obtained Congjian's head and presented it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhou prefect Li Shiwang offered rebels a chance to redeem themselves by hunting one another down. Several hundred who surrendered produced Congjian's head and presented it.

sentences.zh: 諸將還越，式大置酒。

translations.literal: The generals returned to Yue; Shi held a great feast.
translations.idiomatic: When the generals returned to Yue, Shi held a great banquet.

sentences.zh: 諸將乃請曰：「謀等生長軍中，久更行陳，今年得從公破賊，然私有所不諭者，敢問：公之始至，軍食方急，而遽散以賑貧乏，何也？」

translations.literal: The generals then asked: "We grew up in the army and long served in the ranks. This year we followed you in defeating the rebels, yet privately there are matters we do not understand—we venture to ask: When you first arrived, army provisions were urgent, yet you immediately distributed them to relieve the poor—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The generals then asked, "We were raised in the army and have long marched in the field. This year we followed you to defeat the rebels, yet there are things we still do not understand. When you first arrived, provisions were scarce, yet you immediately gave food to the poor—why?

sentences.zh: 式曰：「此易知耳，賊聚谷以誘饑人，吾給之食，則彼不為盜矣；

translations.literal: Shi said: "That is easy to understand. The rebels hoard grain to lure the hungry. If we feed them, they will not become bandits;
translations.idiomatic: Shi replied, "That is simple. The rebels stockpiled grain to draw the hungry to them. Feed the people, and they will not turn to banditry.

sentences.zh: 且諸縣無守兵，賊至，則倉谷適足資之耳」又問：「不置烽燧，何也？」

translations.literal: moreover, the districts have no garrison troops; when rebels arrive, stored grain would simply supply them." They asked again: "Why did you not set beacon fires?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, the counties had no garrison. If rebels came, the stored grain would only supply them." They asked again, "Why did you not set beacon fires?

sentences.zh: 式曰：「烽燧所以趣救兵也，兵盡行，城中無兵以繼之，徒驚士民，使自潰亂耳。」

translations.literal: Shi said: "Beacon fires are to summon relief troops. When all troops march out, the city has no troops to follow up—this only alarms the populace and makes them collapse in disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "Beacon fires summon relief. If every soldier marched out, the city would have no reserve force. That would only panic the people and send them fleeing in disorder.

sentences.zh: 又問：「使懦卒為候騎而少給兵，何也？」

translations.literal: They asked again: "Why did you use cowardly soldiers as scouts and give them few troops?"
translations.idiomatic: They asked again, "Why did you use timid soldiers as scouts and give them so few men?

sentences.zh: 式曰：「彼勇卒操利兵，遇敵且不量力而斗；

translations.literal: Shi said: "Brave soldiers bearing sharp weapons, meeting the enemy, will fight without gauging their strength;
translations.idiomatic: Shi said, "Brave men with sharp weapons will fight the enemy without counting the odds.

sentences.zh: 斗死，則賊至不知矣。」

translations.literal: Once they die fighting, the army will not know the rebels have arrived."
translations.idiomatic: If they die in a skirmish, the main force will never know the rebels are coming.

sentences.zh: 皆拜曰：「非所及也！」

translations.literal: All bowed and said, "Not within our reach!"
translations.idiomatic: They all bowed and said, "We could never have thought of that!"

sentences.zh: 封憲宗子心丐為信王。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong's son Xingai was enfeoffed as Prince of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong's son Xingai was enfeoffed as Prince Xin.

sentences.zh: 八月，裘甫至京師，斬於東市。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Qiu Fu reached the capital and was executed at the Eastern Market.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Qiu Fu reached the capital and was executed at the Eastern Market.

sentences.zh: 加王式檢校右散騎常侍，諸將官賞各有差。

translations.literal: Wang Shi was promoted to Acting Right Cavalry-in-Ordinary; the generals received rewards according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shi was promoted to Acting Right Cavalry-in-Ordinary, and the generals were rewarded according to their merits.

sentences.zh: 先是，上每以越盜為憂，夏侯孜曰：「王式才有餘，不日告捷矣。」

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor often worried about the Yue bandits. Xia Houzi said, "Wang Shi has talent to spare; before long he will report victory."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had often fretted over the Yue rebels. Xia Houzi said, "Wang Shi has more than enough ability. He will report victory before long.

sentences.zh: 孜與式書曰：「公專以執裘甫為事，軍須細大，此期悉力。」

translations.literal: Zhi wrote Shi: "Devote yourself solely to capturing Qiu Fu. Great and small military needs—this office will exert every effort."
translations.idiomatic: Zhi wrote to Shi, "Focus entirely on capturing Qiu Fu. Whatever supplies you need, great or small, this office will provide.

sentences.zh: 故式所奏求無不從，由是能成其功。

translations.literal: Therefore every request Shi's memorials made was granted without refusal, and thus he could accomplish his triumph.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this, every request in Shi's memorials was granted, and he was able to complete the campaign.

sentences.zh: 衛王灌薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Wei Wang Guan died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wei Wang Guan died.

sentences.zh: 九月，白敏中五上表辭位，辛亥，以敏中為司徒、中書令。

translations.literal: Ninth month, Bai Minzhong five times submitted memorials resigning his office; on the day xinhai, Minzhong was made Minister of Education and Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Bai Minzhong submitted five memorials asking to resign. On xinhai he was made Minister of Education and Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，右拾遺句容劉鄴上言：「李德裕父子為相，有聲跡功效，竄逐以來，血屬將盡，生涯已空，宜賜哀閔，贈以一官。」

translations.literal: On the day guiyou, Right Palace Remonstrator Liu Ye of Jurong submitted a statement: "Li Deyu father and son served as chief ministers with noted achievements. Since their banishment, blood relations are nearly extinct and livelihoods emptied—they deserve compassion; grant a posthumous office."
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou, Right Palace Remonstrator Liu Ye of Jurong submitted a memorial saying that Li Deyu and his son had served as chief ministers with distinction, but since their exile their kin were nearly gone and their households ruined. They deserved compassion, he said, and should be granted an office.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁亥，敕復李德裕太子少保、衛國公，贈左僕射。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on the day dinghai, an edict restored Li Deyu as Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince and Duke of Weiguo, posthumously Minister of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on dinghai, an edict restored Li Deyu as Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince and Duke of Weiguo and posthumously made him Minister of the Left.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，以門下侍郎、同平章事夏侯孜同平章事，充西川節度使。

translations.literal: On the day yihai, Junior Director of the Chancellery and Co-Equal Grand Counselor Xia Houzi was made Co-Equal Grand Counselor and Military Commissioner of Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Junior Director of the Chancellery and Co-Equal Grand Counselor Xia Houzi was appointed Co-Equal Grand Counselor and Military Commissioner of Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 以戶部尚書、判度支畢諴為禮部尚書、同平章事。

translations.literal: Minister of Revenue and Comptroller of the Budget Bi Yan was made Minister of Rites and Co-Equal Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue and Comptroller of the Budget Bi Yan was made Minister of Rites and Co-Equal Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 安南都護李鄠復取播州。

translations.literal: Protector-General of Annan Li E recovered Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Protector-General of Annan Li E recaptured Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁丑，上祀圓丘；

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on the day dingchou, the emperor performed the Round Mound sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dingchou, the emperor sacrificed at the Round Mound;

sentences.zh: 赦，改元。

translations.literal: amnesty was granted and the era name changed.
translations.idiomatic: he issued an amnesty and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 十二月，戊申，安南土蠻引南詔兵合三萬餘人乘虛攻交趾，陷之。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on the day wushen, indigenous tribes of Annan led Nanzhao troops totaling more than thirty thousand to exploit the void and attack Jiaozhi; it fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on wushen, indigenous tribes of Annan led more than thirty thousand Nanzhao troops in a surprise attack on Jiaozhi and took the city.

sentences.zh: 都護李鄠與監軍奔武州。

translations.literal: Protector-General Li E and the army supervisor fled to Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Protector-General Li E and the army supervisor fled to Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 懿宗昭聖恭惠孝皇帝上咸通二年（

translations.literal: Emperor Yizong Zhaosheng Gonghui Xiaoxiao, First Year of Xiantong (
translations.idiomatic: Reign of Emperor Yizong of Tang — second year of Xiantong (

sentences.zh: 辛巳，公元八六一年）

translations.literal: xinsi, AD 861)
translations.idiomatic: xinsi, 861 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，詔發邕管及鄰道兵救安南，擊南蠻。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, an edict ordered dispatch of Yongguan and neighboring prefecture troops to rescue Annan and strike the southern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, an edict ordered troops from Yongguan and neighboring circuits to relieve Annan and attack the southern tribes.

sentences.zh: 二月，以中書令白敏中兼中書令，充鳳翔節度使；

translations.literal: Second month, Director of the Chancellery Bai Minzhong was additionally Director of the Chancellery and Military Commissioner of Fengxiang;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Director of the Chancellery Bai Minzhong was additionally made Military Commissioner of Fengxiang;

sentences.zh: 以左僕射、判度支杜悰兼門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Left Minister and Comptroller of the Budget Du Cong was additionally Junior Director of the Chancellery and Co-Equal Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Left Minister and Comptroller of the Budget Du Cong was additionally made Junior Director of the Chancellery and Co-Equal Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 一日，兩樞密使詣中書，宣徽使楊公慶繼至，獨揖悰受宣，三相起，避之西軒。

translations.literal: One day the two Commissioners of Military Affairs came to the Chancellery; Commissioner of the Office of the Palace Ying Yang Gongqing arrived next, bowed to Cong alone to receive the imperial message, and the three chief ministers rose and withdrew to the western portico.
translations.idiomatic: One day the two Commissioners of Military Affairs came to the Chancellery. Palace Commissioner Yang Gongqing arrived next, bowed to Du Cong alone to receive the imperial message, and the three chief ministers rose and withdrew to the western portico.

sentences.zh: 公慶出斜封文書以授悰，發之，乃宣宗大漸時宦官請鄆王監國奏也，且曰：「當時宰相無名者，當以反法處之。」

translations.literal: Gongqing produced a sealed document from an oblique cover and handed it to Cong. When opened, it was the memorial from eunuchs during Emperor Xuanzong's grave illness requesting Prince of Yun as regent, and it said: "The chief ministers who left no names should be punished under the law of treason."
translations.idiomatic: Gongqing produced a sealed document from a side envelope and handed it to Du Cong. Inside was the memorial from eunuchs during Emperor Xuanzong's final illness asking that Prince of Yun be made regent. It also said that any unnamed chief ministers involved should be punished for treason.

sentences.zh: 悰反覆讀良久，曰：「聖主登極，萬方欣戴。

translations.literal: Cong read it repeatedly for a long time and said, "The sage ruler has ascended the throne; the whole realm rejoices in him.
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong read it over and over for a long time, then said, "Our sage sovereign has just taken the throne, and the whole realm rejoices.

sentences.zh: 今日此文書，非臣下所宜窺。」

translations.literal: Today this document is not what subjects should pry into."
translations.idiomatic: This document is not something subjects should be shown.

sentences.zh: 復封以授公慶，曰：「主上欲罪宰相，當於延英面示聖旨，明行誅譴。」

translations.literal: He resealed it and handed it back to Gongqing, saying, "If the sovereign wishes to punish chief ministers, he should personally display the sacred decree in Yanying and openly carry out execution."
translations.idiomatic: He resealed it and returned it to Gongqing, saying, "If His Majesty wishes to punish chief ministers, he should announce the decree in person at Yanying and carry out punishment openly.

sentences.zh: 公慶去，悰復與兩樞密坐，謂曰：「內外之臣，事猶一體，宰相、樞密共參國政。

translations.literal: Gongqing left; Cong sat again with the two Commissioners and said, "Inner and outer ministers are as one body; chief ministers and commissioners jointly participate in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Gongqing left, Du Cong sat down again with the two Commissioners and said, "Ministers inside and outside the palace are one body. Chief ministers and commissioners share in governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 今主上新踐祚，未熟萬機，資內外裨補，固當以仁愛為先，刑殺為後，豈得遽贊成殺宰相事！

translations.literal: Now the sovereign has newly ascended the throne and is not yet familiar with myriad affairs. Inner and outer assistance should take benevolence first and punishments after—how can one hastily endorse killing chief ministers!
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign has only just ascended the throne and does not yet know every affair of state. Inner and outer officials should aid him with benevolence first and punishment last. How can we rush to endorse the execution of chief ministers!

sentences.zh: 若主上習以性成，則中尉、樞密權重禁闈，豈得不自憂乎！

translations.literal: If the sovereign grows accustomed to this by nature, then the Commissioners of the Inner Palace and Military Affairs will wield heavy power within the forbidden gates—will you not worry for yourselves!
translations.idiomatic: If the sovereign grows used to this, the Commissioners of the Inner Palace and Military Affairs will hold unchecked power within the palace. Will you not fear for yourselves?

sentences.zh: 悰受恩六朝，所望致君堯、舜，不欲朝廷以愛憎行法。」

translations.literal: Cong received grace through six reigns; what he hoped was to make the ruler a Yao or Shun; he did not wish the court to administer law by love and hate."
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong had received favor through six reigns. What he hoped was to make the ruler a Yao or a Shun, not to see the court punish men out of personal favor or spite.

sentences.zh: 兩樞密相顧默然，徐曰：「當具以公言白至尊，非公重德，無人及此。」

translations.literal: The two Commissioners looked at each other in silence, then slowly said, "We shall fully report your words to His Majesty. Except for your great virtue, no one could do this."
translations.idiomatic: The two Commissioners looked at each other in silence, then said slowly, "We will report your words fully to His Majesty. No one but a man of your stature could speak as you have.

sentences.zh: 慚悚而退。

translations.literal: They withdrew ashamed and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: They withdrew, ashamed and uneasy.

sentences.zh: 三相復來見悰，微請宣意，悰無言，三相惶怖，乞存家族，悰曰：「勿為他慮。」

translations.literal: The three chief ministers came again to see Cong and subtly asked about the imperial intent; Cong said nothing. The three were terrified and begged to preserve their families. Cong said, "Do not worry about anything else."
translations.idiomatic: The three chief ministers came back to see Du Cong and delicately asked what the emperor intended. Du Cong said nothing. Terrified, they begged him to save their families. He said, "Do not worry.

sentences.zh: 既而寂然，無復宣命。

translations.literal: Afterward all was quiet; no further imperial order came.
translations.idiomatic: After that all was quiet, and no further imperial message came.

sentences.zh: 及延英開，上色甚悅。

translations.literal: When Yanying opened, the emperor's countenance was very pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanying opened, the emperor looked very pleased.

sentences.zh: 是時士大夫深疾宦官，事有小相涉，則眾共棄之，建州進士葉京嘗預宣武軍宴，識監軍之面；

translations.literal: At this time scholar-officials deeply detested eunuchs; if a matter had the slightest connection, all would jointly cast the person out. Jianzhou jinshi Ye Jing had once attended a banquet of the Xuanwu army and recognized the face of the army supervisor;
translations.idiomatic: At that time scholar-officials loathed eunuchs. If anyone had even the slightest connection with them, the whole cohort would cast him out. Jianzhou jinshi Ye Jing had once attended a banquet of the Xuanwu army and recognized the army supervisor's face;

sentences.zh: 既而及第，在長安與同年出遊，遇之於塗，馬上相揖；

translations.literal: Later he passed the jinshi examination; in Chang'an he went out traveling with classmates of the same year, met him on the road, and bowed to each other from horseback;
translations.idiomatic: Later he passed the jinshi examination. While out sightseeing in Chang'an with his classmates, he met the army supervisor on the road and they exchanged bows from horseback.

sentences.zh: 因之謗議喧然，遂沉廢終身，其不相悅如此。

translations.literal: Because of this slander and talk burst forth noisily; he was thus ruined and idle for life—their mutual dislike was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: At once scandalous talk erupted, and he was ruined for life, never to hold office again—such was the depth of their mutual dislike.

sentences.zh: 福王綰薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Fu, Wan, died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Fu, Wan, died.

sentences.zh: 夏，六月，癸丑，以鹽州防禦使王寬為安南經略使，時李鄠自武州收集土軍，攻群蠻，復取安南，朝廷責其失守，貶儋州司戶。

translations.literal: Summer, sixth month, day guichou: Wang Kuan, Defense Commissioner of Yanzhou, was made Protectorate General of Annam. At the time Li E had gathered native troops from Wuzhou, attacked the tribal chiefs, and recovered Annam; the court held him responsible for the prior loss of the territory and demoted him to Registrar of Danzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the sixth month, on the day guichou, Wang Kuan, Defense Commissioner of Yanzhou, was appointed Protectorate General of Annam. Li E had meanwhile rallied native troops from Wuzhou, attacked the tribal chiefs, and retaken Annam, but the court blamed him for the earlier loss of the protectorate and demoted him to Registrar of Danzhou.

sentences.zh: 鄠初至安南，殺蠻酋杜守澄，其宗黨遂誘道群蠻陷交趾，朝廷以杜氏強盛，務在姑息，冀收其力用，乃贈守澄父存誠金吾將軍，再舉鄠殺守澄之罪，長流崖州。

translations.literal: When E had first reached Annam, he killed the tribal chief Du Shoucheng; his clansmen then induced various tribes along the route and seized Jiaozhi. Because the Du clan was powerful, the court sought only to conciliate and hoped to win their service—it posthumously enfeoffed Shoucheng's father Cuncheng as General of the Jinwu Guards, then again charged E with killing Shoucheng and exiled him far to Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Li E first reached Annam, he killed the tribal chief Du Shoucheng. Shoucheng's clansmen then rallied the tribes along the route and seized Jiaozhi. Because the Du clan was powerful, the court chose conciliation over punishment, hoping to win their support—it posthumously enfeoffed Shoucheng's father Cuncheng as General of the Jinwu Guards, then renewed the charge against E for killing Shoucheng and banished him to distant Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，南蠻攻邕州，陷之。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: the southern tribes attacked Yong Prefecture and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the southern tribes attacked Yong Prefecture and captured it.

sentences.zh: 先是，廣、桂、容三道共發兵三千人戍邕州，三年一代。

translations.literal: Earlier, the three circuits of Guang, Gui, and Rong together sent three thousand troops to garrison Yong Prefecture, with relief every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, the Guang, Gui, and Rong circuits had jointly sent three thousand troops to garrison Yong Prefecture, rotating the garrison every three years.

sentences.zh: 經略使段文楚請以三道衣糧自募土軍以代之，朝廷許之，所募才得五百許人。

translations.literal: Protectorate General Duan Wenchu requested to use the clothing and grain allotments of the three circuits to recruit native troops in their place; the court approved it, but the recruits numbered only about five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Protectorate General Duan Wenchu asked to use the clothing and grain funds of the three circuits to recruit native troops in place of the rotating garrisons. The court agreed, but he mustered only about five hundred men.

sentences.zh: 文楚入為金吾將軍，經略使李蒙利其闕額衣糧以自入，悉罷遣三道戍卒，止以所募兵守左、右江，比舊什減七八，故蠻人乘虛入寇。

translations.literal: Wenchu entered the capital as General of the Jinwu Guards; Protectorate General Li Meng pocketed the surplus clothing and grain for himself, dismissed all garrison troops from the three circuits, and kept only the recruited troops to guard the Left and Right Rivers—seven or eight tenths less than before—so the tribes seized the opening and raided.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenchu was transferred to the capital as General of the Jinwu Guards, his successor Li Meng embezzled the surplus clothing and grain, dismissed all garrison troops from the three circuits, and left only the recruits to hold the Left and Right Rivers—barely two or three tenths of the old force. The tribes therefore exploited the weakness and invaded.

sentences.zh: 時蒙已卒，經略使李弘源至鎮才十日，無兵以御之，城陷，弘源與監軍脫身奔蠻州，二十餘日，蠻去，乃還。

translations.literal: By then Meng had already died; Protectorate General Li Hongyuan had been at his post only ten days and had no troops to resist—the city fell. Hongyuan and the army supervisor escaped and fled to Man Prefecture; after more than twenty days the tribes withdrew, and they returned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Meng had already died. His successor Li Hongyuan had been at his post only ten days and had no troops with which to defend the city. When it fell, Hongyuan and the army supervisor fled to Man Prefecture. After more than twenty days the tribes withdrew, and they returned.

sentences.zh: 弘源坐貶建州司戶。

translations.literal: Hongyuan was demoted to Registrar of Jian Prefecture on account of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyuan was demoted to Registrar of Jian Prefecture for the loss.

sentences.zh: 文楚時為殿中監，復以為邕管經略使，至鎮，城邑居人什不存一。

translations.literal: Wenchu was then Director of the Palace Directorate and was again made Protectorate General of Yong Circuit; when he reached his post, scarcely one in ten of the city's inhabitants remained.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Wenchu, then Director of the Palace Directorate, was again appointed Protectorate General of Yong Circuit. When he arrived, scarcely one household in ten remained in the city.

sentences.zh: 文楚，秀實之孫也。

translations.literal: Wenchu was the grandson of Xiushi.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchu was the grandson of Duan Xiushi.

sentences.zh: 杜悰上言：「南詔向化七十年，蜀中寢兵無事，群蠻率服。

translations.literal: Du Cong submitted a memorial: "Nanzhao has turned toward civilization for seventy years; in Shu the armies have rested and all has been peaceful, and the tribal peoples have generally submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Du Cong submitted a memorial: "Nanzhao has been a loyal tributary for seventy years. In Shu the armies have stood down and the frontier has been quiet, and the tribal peoples have generally submitted.

sentences.zh: 今西川兵食單寡，未可輕與之絕，且應遣使弔祭，曉諭清平官等以新王名犯廟諱，故未行冊命，待其更名謝恩，然後遣使刪命，庶全大體。」

translations.literal: Now the armies and provisions of western Shu are few and thin; we must not lightly break with them. We should moreover send envoys to offer condolences, and explain to the Qingpingguan ministers and others that because the new king's name violates a taboo of the ancestral temple, investiture has not yet been carried out; once he changes his name and offers thanks for grace, then send envoys with investiture, so that the larger proprieties may be preserved."
translations.idiomatic: Western Shu now has thin armies and scant provisions, and we must not lightly break with Nanzhao. We should send envoys to offer condolences and explain to the Qingpingguan ministers that because the new king's name violates an imperial taboo, no investiture has yet been issued. Once he changes his name and submits a letter of thanks, we can send envoys to bestow formal investiture and preserve the larger proprieties of the relationship.

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 命左司郎中孟穆為弔祭使。

translations.literal: Meng Mu, Left Section Director in the Ministry of Revenue, was appointed condolence envoy.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Mu, Left Section Director in the Ministry of Revenue, was appointed envoy to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 未發，會南詔寇巂州，攻邛崍關，穆遂不行。

translations.literal: Before he set out, Nanzhao raided Xi Prefecture and attacked the Qionglai Pass, so Mu did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, Nanzhao raided Xi Prefecture and attacked Qionglai Pass, and Mu's mission was canceled.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，以御史大夫鄭涯為山南東道節度使。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Censor-in-Chief Zheng Ya was made Military Governor of Shannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Censor-in-Chief Zheng Ya was appointed Military Governor of Shannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 十一月，加同平章事。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: he was additionally made Co-Equal Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was additionally made Co-Equal Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 懿宗昭聖恭惠孝皇帝上咸通三年（

translations.literal: Above: Emperor Yizong, the Sagely, Respectful, and Gracious Filial Emperor; third year of Xiantong (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yizong, the Sagely, Respectful, and Gracious Filial Emperor; third year of Xiantong (

sentences.zh: 壬午，公元八六二年）

translations.literal: renwu, the year 862 CE)
translations.idiomatic: renwu, 862 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，庚寅朔，群臣上尊號曰睿文明聖孝德皇帝。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day gengyin, new moon: the assembled ministers offered the honorific title Sagely, Civil, Bright, Sacred, Filial, and Virtuous Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on the new moon of the day gengyin, the assembled ministers offered the honorific title Sagely, Civil, Bright, Sacred, Filial, and Virtuous Emperor.

sentences.zh: 赦天下。

translations.literal: An amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 以中書侍郎、同平章事蔣伸同平章事，充河中節度使。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Equal Grand Counselor Jiang Shen was made Co-Equal Grand Counselor and Military Governor of Hezhong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shen, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Equal Grand Counselor, was appointed Military Governor of Hezhong Circuit while retaining his grand counselor title.

sentences.zh: 二月，棣王惴薨。

translations.literal: Second month: Prince of Di, Zhuai, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Prince of Di, Zhuai, died.

sentences.zh: 南詔復寇安南，經略使王寬數來告急，朝廷以前湖南觀察使蔡襲代之，仍發許、滑、徐、汴、荊、襄、潭、鄂等道兵各三萬人授襲以御之。

translations.literal: Nanzhao again raided Annam; Protectorate General Wang Kuan repeatedly sent urgent reports. The court replaced him with former Hunan Observation Commissioner Cai Xi and moreover dispatched thirty thousand troops from each of the circuits of Xu, Hua, Xuzhou, Bian, Jing, Xiang, Tan, and E, placing them under Xi to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao again invaded Annam, and Protectorate General Wang Kuan sent repeated urgent appeals. The court replaced him with the former Hunan Observation Commissioner Cai Xi and dispatched thirty thousand troops from each of the Xu, Hua, Xuzhou, Bian, Jing, Xiang, Tan, and E circuits, placing them under Xi for the defense.

sentences.zh: 兵勢既盛，蠻遂引去。

translations.literal: Once the military strength was great, the tribes withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the assembled force grew strong, the tribes withdrew.

sentences.zh: 邕管經略使段文楚坐變更舊制，左遷威衛將軍、分司。

translations.literal: Protectorate General of Yong Circuit Duan Wenchu was demoted to General of the Weiwu Guards with a nominal post in the capital on account of changing the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Wenchu, Protectorate General of Yong Circuit, was demoted to General of the Weiwu Guards with a nominal capital post for having altered the old garrison system.

sentences.zh: 左庶子蔡京，性貪虐多詐，時相以為有吏才，奏遣制置嶺南事。

translations.literal: Left Household Companion Cai Jing was by nature greedy, cruel, and full of deceit; the chief ministers considered him to have administrative talent and memorialized to dispatch him to oversee Lingnan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing, Left Household Companion, was greedy, cruel, and deceitful by nature. The chief ministers considered him an able administrator and memorialized to send him to oversee affairs in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 三月，京還，奏事稱旨，復以京權知太僕卿，充荊襄以南宣慰安撫使。

translations.literal: Third month: Jing returned and reported on affairs to the emperor's satisfaction; he was again made Acting Grand Master of the Stud and Commissioner for Pacification and Reassurance south of Jing and Xiang.
