translations.idiomatic: In the third month Cai Jing returned and reported to the emperor's satisfaction. He was again made Acting Grand Master of the Stud and Commissioner for Pacification and Reassurance south of Jing and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，己亥朔，敕於兩街四寺各置戒壇，度人三七日。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, day jihai, new moon: an edict ordered ordination platforms set up at four monasteries on the two avenues, with ordinations conducted over twenty-one days.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on the new moon of the day jihai, an edict ordered ordination platforms erected at four monasteries on the two avenues, with ordinations to be conducted over twenty-one days.

sentences.zh: 上奉佛太過，怠於政事，嘗於咸泰殿築壇為內寺尼受戒，兩街僧、尼皆入預；

translations.literal: The emperor honored Buddhism excessively and was slack in government affairs; he once built a platform in the Xiantai Hall to ordain palace nuns, and monks and nuns from both avenues all entered to participate;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor honored Buddhism to excess and neglected government affairs. He once built an ordination platform in Xiantai Hall to ordain palace nuns, with monks and nuns from both avenues all taking part;

sentences.zh: 又於禁中設講席，自唱經，手錄梵夾；

translations.literal: he also set up lecture seats within the palace, chanted sutras himself, and copied Buddhist texts by hand;
translations.idiomatic: he also set up lecture seats within the palace, chanted sutras himself, and copied Buddhist texts by hand;

sentences.zh: 又數幸諸寺，施與無度。

translations.literal: and again and again visited various monasteries, bestowing gifts without limit.
translations.idiomatic: and repeatedly visited monasteries, lavishing gifts without measure.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎蕭倣上疏，以為：「玄祖之道，慈儉為先；

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel Xiao Fang submitted a memorial, stating: "The Way of the Mysterious Ancestor takes compassion and frugality as foremost;
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Personnel Xiao Fang submitted a memorial, stating: "The Way of the Mysterious Ancestor puts compassion and frugality first;

sentences.zh: 素王之風，仁義為首，垂范百代，必不可加。

translations.literal: the style of the uncrowned king puts benevolence and righteousness first—a model for a hundred generations, to which nothing may be added.
translations.idiomatic: the example of the sage-king puts benevolence and righteousness first—a model for a hundred generations that nothing can surpass.

sentences.zh: 佛者，棄位出家，割愛中之至難，取滅後之殊勝，非帝王所宜慕也。

translations.literal: The Buddha abandoned rank and left home, cutting the hardest ties within affection to obtain the extraordinary blessings after extinction—this is not what an emperor should admire.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha abandoned rank and left home, severing the deepest ties of affection to seek blessings beyond this life. That is not a path an emperor should emulate.

sentences.zh: 願陛下時開延英，接對四輔，力求人瘼，虔奉宗祧。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will regularly open Yanying, receive the four chief ministers, strive to learn the people's afflictions, and devoutly serve the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: I pray that Your Majesty will regularly convene court at Yanying, receive the four chief ministers, strive to learn the people's afflictions, and devoutly tend the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 思繆賞與濫刑，其殃必至；

translations.literal: Reflect on extravagant rewards and indiscriminate punishments—their calamity is sure to come;
translations.idiomatic: Beware of extravagant rewards and reckless punishments, for their calamity is sure to follow;

sentences.zh: 知勝殘而去殺，得福甚多。

translations.literal: know that overcoming cruelty and abandoning killing brings very great blessing.
translations.idiomatic: know that to overcome cruelty and renounce killing brings great blessing.

sentences.zh: 罷去講筵，躬勤政事。」

translations.literal: Abolish the lecture sessions and personally attend diligently to government affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Dismiss the lecture sessions and devote yourself personally to governing the realm.

sentences.zh: 上雖嘉獎，竟不能從。

translations.literal: Although the emperor praised this, in the end he could not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised the memorial, but in the end he did not follow its advice.

sentences.zh: 嶺南舊分五管，廣、桂、邕、容、安南，皆隸嶺南節度使；

translations.literal: Lingnan was formerly divided into five administrations—Guang, Gui, Yong, Rong, and Annam—all subordinate to the Military Governor of Lingnan;
translations.idiomatic: Lingnan had formerly been divided into five administrations—Guang, Gui, Yong, Rong, and Annam—all subordinate to the Military Governor of Lingnan;

sentences.zh: 蔡京奏請分嶺南為兩道節度，從之。

translations.literal: Cai Jing memorialized requesting that Lingnan be divided into two military circuits; this was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing memorialized to divide Lingnan into two military circuits, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 五月，敕以廣州為東道，邕州為西道，又割桂管龔、像二州，容管籐、巖二州隸邕管。

translations.literal: Fifth month: an edict made Guang Prefecture the East Circuit and Yong Prefecture the West Circuit, and further detached Gong and Xiang prefectures from Gui Circuit and Teng and Yan prefectures from Rong Circuit, placing them under Yong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month an edict made Guang Prefecture the East Circuit and Yong Prefecture the West Circuit. Gong and Xiang prefectures were detached from Gui Circuit, and Teng and Yan prefectures from Rong Circuit, and all were placed under Yong Circuit.

sentences.zh: 尋以嶺南節度使韋宙為東道節度使，以蔡京為西道節度使。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Military Governor of Lingnan Wei Zhou was made Military Governor of the East Circuit, and Cai Jing was made Military Governor of the West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Wei Zhou, Military Governor of Lingnan, was appointed Military Governor of the East Circuit, and Cai Jing was made Military Governor of the West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 蔡襲將諸道兵在安南，蔡京忌之，恐其立功，奏稱：「南蠻遠遁，邊徼無虞，武夫邀功，妄占戍兵，虛費饋運。

translations.literal: Cai Xi commanded the troops of the various circuits in Annam; Cai Jing envied him, fearing he would win merit, and memorialized: "The southern tribes have fled far away; the frontier is without worry. Military men seek merit, falsely retaining garrison troops and wasting transport supplies in vain.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xi commanded the allied forces in Annam. Cai Jing envied him and feared he would win glory, so he memorialized: "The southern tribes have withdrawn far away and the frontier is secure. Military men are seeking credit, falsely holding on to garrison troops and wasting transport supplies.

sentences.zh: 蓋以荒陬路遠，難於覆驗，故得肆其奸詐。

translations.literal: Because the wild borderlands are distant and hard to verify on the spot, they are able to indulge their fraud at will.
translations.idiomatic: Because the frontier is remote and hard to verify, they are free to indulge their fraud.

sentences.zh: 請罷戍兵，各還本道。」

translations.literal: I request that the garrison troops be dismissed and each return to its home circuit."
translations.idiomatic: I request that the garrison troops be dismissed and sent back to their home circuits.

sentences.zh: 朝廷從之。

translations.literal: The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 襲累奏稱群蠻伺隙日久，不可無備，乞留戍兵五千人。

translations.literal: Xi repeatedly memorialized that the tribal chiefs had long watched for openings and could not be left unguarded; he begged to retain five thousand garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xi repeatedly memorialized that the tribes had long watched for an opening and that the frontier could not be left undefended. He asked to retain five thousand garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: This was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 襲以蠻寇必至，交趾兵食皆闕，謀力兩窮，作十必死狀申中書。

translations.literal: Xi, believing tribal raiders were sure to come and that troops and provisions in Jiaozhi were both lacking, was exhausted in counsel and strength; he submitted ten memorials declaring certain death to the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Convinced that a tribal invasion was imminent and that Jiaozhi lacked both troops and provisions, Cai Xi was at the end of his resources. He submitted ten memorials to the Chancellery declaring that defeat was certain.

sentences.zh: 時相信京之言，終不之省。

translations.literal: The court at the time trusted Jing's words and never looked into the matter.
translations.idiomatic: The court trusted Cai Jing and never investigated further.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，徐州軍亂，逐節度使溫璋。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: the army of Xuzhou mutinied and drove out Military Governor Wen Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, the Xuzhou army mutinied and drove out Military Governor Wen Zhang.

sentences.zh: 初，王智興既得徐州，募勇悍之士二千人，號銀刀、雕旗、門槍、挾馬等七軍，常以三百餘人自衛，露刃坐於兩廡夾幕之下，每月一更。

translations.literal: Initially, after Wang Zhixing took Xuzhou, he recruited two thousand fierce and bold men in seven armies called Silver Blade, Carved Banner, Gate Spear, Flanking Horse, and others; he regularly kept more than three hundred for his personal guard, sitting with bared blades beneath the covered corridors on both sides, rotating monthly.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Zhixing seized Xuzhou, he recruited two thousand fierce fighters organized into seven corps—the Silver Blade, Carved Banner, Gate Spear, Flanking Horse, and others. More than three hundred of them served as his personal guard, sitting with drawn blades beneath the covered corridors on both sides of the hall, rotating each month.

sentences.zh: 其後節度使多儒臣，其兵浸驕，小不如意，一夫大呼，其眾皆和之，節度使輒自後門逃去。

translations.literal: Afterward most military governors were scholar-officials; the troops grew increasingly arrogant. At the slightest displeasure one man would shout loudly and the whole host would join in, and the military governor would flee out the back gate.
translations.idiomatic: Later military governors were mostly scholar-officials, and the troops grew ever more arrogant. At the slightest grievance one man would shout and the whole host would join in, and the governor would flee out the back gate.

sentences.zh: 前節度使田牟至與之雜坐飲酒，把臂拊背，或為之執板唱歌。

translations.literal: Former Military Governor Tian Mou would sit and drink mixed among them, clasp arms and pat backs, or hold the clapper and sing for them.
translations.idiomatic: The former governor Tian Mou would sit and drink among them, clasp their arms and clap their backs, and sometimes beat time and sing for them himself.

sentences.zh: 犒賜之費，日以萬計，風雨寒暑，復加勞來，猶時喧嘩，邀求不已。

translations.literal: The cost of rewards and gifts ran to tens of thousands per day; through wind, rain, cold, and heat he still added further courtesies, yet they still clamored from time to time and demanded without end.
translations.idiomatic: Rewards and gifts cost tens of thousands each day. Through wind, rain, cold, and heat he continued to court them, yet they still clamored and demanded without end.

sentences.zh: 牟薨，璋代之，驕兵素聞璋性嚴，憚之。

translations.literal: When Mou died, Zhang replaced him; the arrogant troops had long heard that Zhang's nature was stern and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Mou died, Wen Zhang replaced him. The mutinous troops had long heard that Zhang was stern by nature and feared him.

sentences.zh: 璋開懷慰撫，而驕兵終懷猜忌，賜酒食皆不歷口，一旦，竟聚噪而逐之。

translations.literal: Zhang opened his heart and comforted them, but the arrogant troops remained suspicious in the end; wine and food he bestowed they would not pass their lips. One day they suddenly gathered, clamored, and drove him out.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang tried to reassure them openly, but the mutinous troops remained suspicious and would not touch the wine and food he offered. One day they suddenly gathered, raised a clamor, and drove him out.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知璋無辜，乙亥，以璋為邠寧節度使，以浙東觀察使王式為武寧節度使。

translations.literal: The court knew Zhang was innocent; on the day yihai Zhang was made Military Governor of Binning Circuit, and Zhedong Observation Commissioner Wang Shi was made Military Governor of Wuning Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that Zhang was innocent, the court on the day yihai appointed him Military Governor of Binning Circuit and named Wang Shi, Zhedong Observation Commissioner, Military Governor of Wuning Circuit.

sentences.zh: 以前西川節度使、同平章事夏侯孜為左僕射、同平章事。

translations.literal: Former Military Governor of Xichuan Circuit and Co-Equal Grand Counselor Xiahou Zi was made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Co-Equal Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: The former Military Governor of Xichuan Circuit and Co-Equal Grand Counselor Xiahou Zi was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Co-Equal Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 忠武、義成兩軍從王式討裘甫者猶在浙東，詔式帥以赴徐州，驕兵聞之，甚懼。

translations.literal: The Zhongwu and Yicheng armies that had followed Wang Shi against Qiu Fu were still in Zhedong; an edict ordered Shi to lead them to Xuzhou, and when the arrogant troops heard this they were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhongwu and Yicheng armies that had followed Wang Shi against Qiu Fu were still in Zhedong. An edict ordered Shi to lead them to Xuzhou, and the mutinous troops were greatly afraid when they heard it.

sentences.zh: 八月，式至大彭館，始出迎謁。

translations.literal: Eighth month: Shi reached the Da Peng hostel and only then went out to receive and greet them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Wang Shi reached the Da Peng hostel and only then went out to receive the troops.

sentences.zh: 式視事三日，饗兩鎮將士，遣還。

translations.literal: Shi assumed office for three days, feasted the officers and soldiers of the two circuits, and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: After three days in office, Wang Shi feasted the officers and soldiers of the two circuits and sent them back to camp.

sentences.zh: 既擐甲執兵，命圍驕兵，盡殺之，銀刀都將邵澤等數千人皆死。

translations.literal: Once they had donned armor and taken up weapons, he ordered the arrogant troops surrounded and all killed; several thousand including Silver Blade commander Shao Ze all died.
translations.idiomatic: Once the allied troops had donned armor and taken up arms, he ordered the mutinous corps surrounded and slaughtered. Several thousand men, including Silver Blade commander Shao Ze, were killed.

sentences.zh: 甲子，敕以徐州先隸淄青道，李洧自歸，始置徐海使額。

translations.literal: Day jiazi: an edict stated that Xuzhou had formerly been subordinate to the Ziqing circuit; when Li Wei submitted, the Xu-Hai commissioner post was first established.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiazi an edict recalled that Xuzhou had formerly been subordinate to the Ziqing circuit and that the Xu-Hai commissioner post had been established when Li Wei submitted.

sentences.zh: 及張建封以威名寵任，特帖濠、泗二州。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jianfeng was favored and entrusted because of his martial renown, Hao and Si prefectures were specially attached.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jianfeng was favored for his martial renown, Hao and Si prefectures were specially attached to his command.

sentences.zh: 當時本以控扼淄青、光蔡。

translations.literal: At the time this was originally to control and restrain Ziqing and Guang-Cai.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the arrangement had been intended to check Ziqing and Guang-Cai.

sentences.zh: 自寇孽消弭，而武寧一道職為亂階。

translations.literal: Since bandit troubles were extinguished, the Wuning circuit alone served as the ladder to rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Once the rebel threat had passed, the Wuning circuit alone became a seedbed of mutiny.

sentences.zh: 今改為徐州團練使，隸兗海節度。

translations.literal: Now it is changed to a Xuzhou Training and Defense Commissioner, subordinate to the Yan-Hai Military Governor.
translations.idiomatic: It was now reduced to a Xuzhou Training and Defense Commissioner subordinate to the Yan-Hai Military Governor.

sentences.zh: 復以濠州歸淮南道，更於宿州置宿泗都團練觀察使。

translations.literal: Hao Prefecture is again returned to the Huainan circuit; a Su-Si Training, Defense, and Observation Commissioner is newly established at Su Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Prefecture was returned to Huainan Circuit, and a Su-Si Training, Defense, and Observation Commissioner was established at Su Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 留將士二千人守徐州，餘皆分隸兗、宿。

translations.literal: Two thousand officers and soldiers are left to guard Xuzhou; the rest are all distributed to Yan and Su.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand officers and soldiers were left to garrison Xuzhou; the rest were distributed between Yan and Su.

sentences.zh: 且以王式為武寧節度使，兼徐、泗、濠、宿制置使。

translations.literal: Moreover Wang Shi is made Military Governor of Wuning Circuit and concurrently Commissioner for Arrangement of Xu, Si, Hao, and Su.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shi was also made Military Governor of Wuning Circuit and concurrently Commissioner for Arrangement of Xu, Si, Hao, and Su.

sentences.zh: 委式與監軍楊玄質分配將士赴諸道訖，然後將忠武、義成兩道兵至汴滑，各遣歸本道，身詣京師。

translations.literal: Shi and Army Supervisor Yang Xuanzhi were entrusted to assign officers and soldiers to the various circuits; when that was done, he then led the Zhongwu and Yicheng troops to Bian and Hua, sent each back to its home circuit, and went in person to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shi and Army Supervisor Yang Xuanzhi were charged with assigning the troops to their circuits. When that was finished, he led the Zhongwu and Yicheng forces to Bian and Hua, sent each army back to its home circuit, and went to the capital himself.

sentences.zh: 其銀刀等軍逃匿將士，聽一月內自首，一切勿問。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers of the Silver Blade and other armies who had fled and hidden were permitted to surrender within one month without any inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers of the Silver Blade and other corps who had fled were permitted to surrender within one month without punishment.

sentences.zh: 嶺南西道節度使蔡京為政苛慘，設砲烙之刑，闔境怨之，遂為邕州軍士所逐，奔籐州，詐為敕書及攻討使印，募鄉丁及旁側土軍以入邕州。

translations.literal: Military Governor of Lingnan West Circuit Cai Jing governed with harsh cruelty and established branding-iron torture; the whole territory resented him, and he was driven out by soldiers of Yong Prefecture. He fled to Teng Prefecture, forged an imperial edict and the seal of a punitive commissioner, and recruited local militia and nearby native troops to enter Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing, Military Governor of Lingnan West Circuit, ruled with harsh cruelty and instituted branding-iron torture. The whole region hated him, and soldiers of Yong Prefecture drove him out. He fled to Teng Prefecture, forged an imperial edict and the seal of a punitive commissioner, and raised local militia and nearby native troops to reenter Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 眾既烏合，會輒潰敗，往依桂州，桂州人怨其分裂，不納。

translations.literal: The host, once gathered like crows, soon collapsed in defeat; he went to rely on Gui Prefecture, but the people of Gui resented his splitting the circuit and would not receive him.
translations.idiomatic: His ragtag force soon collapsed in defeat. He fled toward Gui Prefecture, but the people there resented his role in splitting the circuit and refused to take him in.

sentences.zh: 京無所自容。

translations.literal: Jing had nowhere to contain himself.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Jing had nowhere left to turn.

sentences.zh: 敕貶崖州司戶，不肯之官，還，至零陵，敕賜自盡。

translations.literal: An edict demoted him to Registrar of Yazhou; he refused to take up the post. On his return, when he reached Lingling, an edict granted him death by his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: An edict demoted him to Registrar of Yazhou, but he refused to take up the post. On his way back, when he reached Lingling, an edict ordered him to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 以桂管觀察使鄭愚為嶺南西道節度使。

translations.literal: Gui Circuit Observation Commissioner Zheng Yu was made Military Governor of Lingnan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yu, Observation Commissioner of Gui Circuit, was appointed Military Governor of Lingnan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙申朔，立皇子佾為魏王，侹為涼王，佶為蜀王。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day bingshen, new moon: the emperor's sons Yi was enfeoffed as Prince of Wei, Ting as Prince of Liang, and Ji as Prince of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on the new moon of the day bingshen, the emperor's sons Yi, Ting, and Ji were enfeoffed as Princes of Wei, Liang, and Shu respectively.

sentences.zh: 十一月，立順宗子緝為蘄王，憲宗子憤為榮王。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: Emperor Shunzong's son Ji was enfeoffed as Prince of Qi, and Emperor Xianzong's son Fen as Prince of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Emperor Shunzong's son Ji was enfeoffed as Prince of Qi, and Emperor Xianzong's son Fen as Prince of Rong.

sentences.zh: 南詔帥群蠻五萬寇安南，都護蔡襲告急，敕發荊南、湖南兩道兵二千，桂管義征子弟三千，詣邕州受鄭愚節度。

translations.literal: Nanzhao led fifty thousand tribal troops to raid Annam; Protector-General Cai Xi sent urgent reports. An edict dispatched two thousand troops from the Jingnan and Hunan circuits and three thousand volunteer sons and younger brothers from Gui Circuit, to proceed to Yong Prefecture and accept Zheng Yu's command.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao led fifty thousand tribal warriors against Annam, and Protector-General Cai Xi sent urgent appeals for help. An edict dispatched two thousand troops from the Jingnan and Hunan circuits and three thousand volunteer recruits from Gui Circuit to Yong Prefecture under Zheng Yu's command.

sentences.zh: 嶺南東道節度使韋宙奏：「蠻寇必向邕州，若不先保護，遽欲遠征，恐蠻於後乘虛扼絕餉道。」

translations.literal: Military Governor of Lingnan East Circuit Wei Zhou memorialized: "The tribal raiders are sure to move toward Yong Prefecture; if we do not protect it first and hastily seek a distant campaign, I fear the tribes will afterward seize the opening and cut off the supply route."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhou, Military Governor of Lingnan East Circuit, memorialized: "The raiders are sure to strike toward Yong Prefecture. If we do not secure it first and rush into a distant campaign, the tribes may exploit the opening behind us and cut our supply lines.

sentences.zh: 乃敕蔡襲屯海門，鄭愚分兵備御。

translations.literal: An edict then ordered Cai Xi to encamp at Haimen, and Zheng Yu to divide troops for defense.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Cai Xi to encamp at Haimen while Zheng Yu divided his forces for defense.

sentences.zh: 十二月，襲又求益兵，敕山南東道發弩手千人赴之。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Xi again requested additional troops; an edict ordered Shannan East Circuit to dispatch one thousand crossbowmen to join him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Cai Xi again requested reinforcements, and an edict ordered Shannan East Circuit to send one thousand crossbowmen to his aid.

sentences.zh: 時南詔已圍交趾，襲嬰城固守，救兵不得至。

translations.literal: At the time Nanzhao had already besieged Jiaozhi; Xi closed the city and held fast, but relief troops could not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: By then Nanzhao had already besieged Jiaozhi. Cai Xi held the city, but relief troops could not reach him.

sentences.zh: 翼王彈薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Yi, Tan, died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yi, Tan, died.

sentences.zh: 是歲，嗢末始入貢。

translations.literal: This year the Wamo first sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Wamo first sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 嗢末者，吐蕃之奴號也。

translations.literal: The Wamo were the slave designation of the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: The Wamo were so called because they had been slaves of the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃每發兵，其富室多以奴從，往往一家至十數人，由是吐蕃之眾多。

translations.literal: Whenever the Tibetans raised troops, wealthy households mostly followed with slaves; often one household would bring ten or more, and thus Tibetan numbers were great.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Tibet raised troops, wealthy households commonly brought slaves in their train—often ten or more from a single household—so Tibetan armies swelled in number.

sentences.zh: 及論恐熱作亂，奴多無主，遂相糾合為部落，散在甘、肅、瓜、沙、河、渭、岷、廓、疊、宕之間。

translations.literal: When Lun Gongren rebelled, many slaves were left without masters; they then gathered one another into tribal groups, scattered among Gan, Su, Gua, Sha, He, Wei, Min, Kuo, Die, and Dang.
translations.idiomatic: When Lun Gongren rebelled, many slaves were left masterless. They banded together into tribal groups scattered across Gan, Su, Gua, Sha, He, Wei, Min, Kuo, Die, and Dang.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃微弱者反依附之。

translations.literal: Weakened Tibetans in turn attached themselves to them.
translations.idiomatic: Weaker Tibetans in turn attached themselves to them.

sentences.zh: 懿宗昭聖恭惠孝皇帝上咸通四年（

translations.literal: Above: Emperor Yizong, the Sagely, Respectful, and Gracious Filial Emperor; fourth year of Xiantong (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yizong, the Sagely, Respectful, and Gracious Filial Emperor; fourth year of Xiantong (

sentences.zh: 癸未，公元八六三年）

translations.literal: guiwei, the year 863 CE)
translations.idiomatic: guiwei, 863 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月。

translations.literal: Spring, first month.
translations.idiomatic: Spring, first month.

sentences.zh: 庚午，上祀圓丘；

translations.literal: Day gengwu: the emperor sacrificed at the Round Mound;
translations.idiomatic: On the day gengwu the emperor sacrificed at the Round Mound;

sentences.zh: 赦天下。

translations.literal: An amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.

sentences.zh: 是日，南詔陷交趾。

translations.literal: That same day, Nanzhao captured Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: That same day, Nanzhao took Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 蔡襲左右皆盡，徒步力戰，身集十矢，欲趣監軍船，船已離岸，遂溺海死。

translations.literal: Cai Xi's attendants were all exhausted; he fought on foot with all his strength, his body taking ten arrows. He tried to reach the military supervisor's ship, but the ship had already left shore, and he drowned in the sea and died.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xi's attendants were all killed. Fighting on foot with his last strength, his body pierced by ten arrows, he tried to reach the military supervisor's ship—but it had already put to sea—and drowned.

sentences.zh: 幕僚樊綽攜其印浮度江。

translations.literal: Staff officer Fan Chuo carried his seal and floated across the river.
translations.idiomatic: The staff officer Fan Chuo swam the river carrying Cai Xi's official seal.

sentences.zh: 荊南、江西、鄂岳、襄州將士四百餘人，走至城東水際，荊南虞候元惟德等謂眾曰：「吾輩無船，入水則死，不若還向城與蠻鬥，人以一身易二蠻，亦為有利。」

translations.literal: More than four hundred officers and soldiers of Jingnan, Jiangxi, Eyue, and Xiang Prefectures fled to the water's edge east of the city. Jingnan defense officer Yuan Weide and others said to the crowd: "We have no boats; if we enter the water we die. Better to turn back toward the city and fight the barbarians—one man exchanging himself for two barbarians is also profitable."
translations.idiomatic: More than four hundred officers and soldiers from Jingnan, Jiangxi, Eyue, and Xiangzhou fled to the waterfront east of the city. Yuan Weide, a defense officer of Jingnan, addressed the men: "We have no boats—take to the water and we die. Better to turn back into the city and fight the barbarians. Trade one of our lives for two of theirs, and the exchange still favors us."

sentences.zh: 遂還向城，入東羅門。

translations.literal: They then turned back toward the city and entered the East Luomen Gate.
translations.idiomatic: They turned back toward the city and entered through the East Luomen Gate.

sentences.zh: 蠻不為備；

translations.literal: The barbarians were unprepared;
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians were caught unprepared;

sentences.zh: 惟德等縱兵殺蠻二千餘人。

translations.literal: Yuan Weide and the others released their troops and killed more than two thousand barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Weide and his men charged and killed more than two thousand of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 逮夜，蠻將楊思縉始自子城出救之，惟德等皆死。

translations.literal: By nightfall, the barbarian general Yang Sijin finally came out from the inner citadel to rescue them; Yuan Weide and the others all died.
translations.idiomatic: By nightfall the Nanzhao commander Yang Sijin finally sallied from the inner citadel to the relief, and Yuan Weide and his men were all killed.

sentences.zh: 南詔兩陷交趾，所殺虜且十五萬人。

translations.literal: Nanzhao twice captured Jiaozhi; those killed and captured amounted to nearly one hundred fifty thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: In two assaults on Jiaozhi, Nanzhao killed and captured nearly a hundred and fifty thousand people.

sentences.zh: 留兵二萬，使思縉據交趾城。

translations.literal: They left twenty thousand troops, appointing Sijin to hold Jiaozhi city.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty thousand troops were left behind under Yang Sijin to hold Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 谿洞夷獠無遠近皆降之。

translations.literal: Tribal peoples of the streams and caves, near and far, all submitted to them.
translations.idiomatic: Stream-dwellers and tribal peoples near and far all submitted to Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 詔諸道兵赴安南者悉召還，分保嶺南東、西道。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all troops from the various circuits bound for Annam to be recalled entirely, and distributed to garrison the Eastern and Western Lingnan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled all troops from the various circuits that had been marching to Annam and redeployed them to defend the Eastern and Western Lingnan circuits.

sentences.zh: 上游宴無節，左拾遺劉蛻上疏曰：「今西涼築城，應接未決於與奪。

translations.literal: At court feasting was unrestrained. Left Reminder Liu Tui submitted a memorial saying: "Now fortifications are being built at Xiliang, and the decision to seize or relinquish is still unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: The court feasted without restraint. Left Reminder Liu Tui submitted a memorial: "Fortifications are going up at Xiliang, yet we still have not decided whether to hold or abandon the position.

sentences.zh: 南蠻侵軼，干戈悉在於道塗。

translations.literal: Southern barbarians are raiding; weapons of war fill the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Southern barbarians are raiding, and the roads are thronged with marching armies.

sentences.zh: 旬月以來，不為無事。

translations.literal: In the past ten days and more, it has not been without affairs.
translations.idiomatic: These past weeks have hardly been uneventful.

sentences.zh: 陛下不形憂閔以示遠近，則何以責其死力！

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not show concern and compassion to those near and far, how can you demand that they exert themselves unto death!
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not show the realm your concern and care, how can you expect men to fight to the death for you?

sentences.zh: 望節娛游，以待遠人乂安，未晚。」

translations.literal: I hope you will restrain pleasure-seeking and wait until distant peoples are settled and at peace—it is not too late."
translations.idiomatic: Restrain your pleasures and wait until the frontier is pacified—it is not yet too late.

sentences.zh: 弗聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to heed him.

sentences.zh: 二月，甲午朔，上歷拜十六陵。

translations.literal: Second month, first day jiawu of the new moon: the emperor in succession visited and paid respects at the sixteen imperial tombs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the first day of the new moon (day jiawu), the emperor paid his respects at all sixteen imperial tombs in turn.

sentences.zh: 置天雄軍天秦州，以成、河、渭三州隸焉。

translations.literal: The Tianxiong Army was established at Tian Qin Prefecture, with Cheng, He, and Wei Prefectures placed under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianxiong Army was established at Tian Qinzhou, with Chengzhou, Hezhou, and Weizhou placed under its command.

sentences.zh: 以前左金吾將軍王晏實為天雄觀察使。

translations.literal: The former Left Golden Guard General Wang Yanshi was appointed Tianxiong observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Former Left Golden Guard General Wang Yanshi was made Tianxiong observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 三月，歸義節度使張義潮奏自將蕃、漢兵七千克復涼州。

translations.literal: Third month: Zhang Yichao, military governor of Guiyi, reported that he personally led seven thousand Tibetan and Han troops to recover Liang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Guiyi military governor Zhang Yichao reported that he had personally led seven thousand mixed Tibetan and Han troops to recover Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 南蠻寇左、右江，浸逼邕州。

translations.literal: Southern barbarians raided the Left and Right Rivers, gradually pressing on Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Southern barbarians raided the Left and Right River regions and drew ever closer to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 鄭愚懼，自言儒臣無將略，請任武臣。

translations.literal: Zheng Yu was afraid; he declared himself a civil official without military strategy and asked that a military official be appointed in his place.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yu, fearing the situation, protested that as a civilian official he lacked military talent and asked that a military man take over.

sentences.zh: 朝廷召義武節度使康承訓詣闕，欲使之代愚，仍詔選軍校數人、士卒數百人自隨。

translations.literal: The court summoned Yiwu military governor Kang Cheng-xun to the capital, intending to have him replace Yu; an edict also directed that he select several military officers and several hundred soldiers to bring with him.
translations.idiomatic: The court summoned Yiwu military governor Kang Cheng-xun to the capital to replace Zheng Yu, ordering him to bring several officers and a few hundred handpicked soldiers.

sentences.zh: 中書侍郎、同平章事畢諴以同列多徇私不法，稱疾辭位。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Secretariat and co–Director of the Chancellery Bi Zan, because many of his colleagues were practicing favoritism in violation of the law, cited illness and resigned his post.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Vice Director and Co-Director of the Chancellery Bi Zan resigned on grounds of illness, citing widespread favoritism and lawlessness among his colleagues.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，罷為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: he was demoted to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he was removed from the chancellorship and made Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，群盜入徐州，殺官吏。

translations.literal: Day gengxu: bandits entered Xuzhou and killed officials.
translations.idiomatic: On day gengxu bandits entered Xuzhou and killed government officials.

sentences.zh: 刺史曹慶討平之。

translations.literal: Prefect Cao Qing suppressed and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Cao Qing suppressed the uprising.

sentences.zh: 康承訓至京師，以為嶺南西道節度使，發荊、襄、洪、鄂四道兵萬人與之俱。

translations.literal: Kang Cheng-xun arrived at the capital and was appointed military governor of Western Lingnan Circuit; ten thousand troops from the four circuits of Jing, Xiang, Hong, and E were mobilized to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: When Kang Cheng-xun reached the capital he was appointed military governor of Western Lingnan, and ten thousand troops from Jing, Xiang, Hong, and E were mobilized to accompany him.

sentences.zh: 五月，戊辰，以翰林學士承旨、兵部侍郎楊收同平章事。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day wuchen: Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance and Vice Minister of War Yang Shou was made co–Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on day wuchen, Hanlin Academician-in-Attendance and Vice Minister of War Yang Shou was made co-director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 收，發之弟也，與左軍中尉楊玄價敘同宗相結，故得為相。

translations.literal: Shou was the younger brother of Yang Fa; he declared kinship with Left Army Commander Yang Xuanjia and formed an alliance, and therefore obtained the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shou was Yang Fa's younger brother; he claimed kinship with Left Army Commander Yang Xuanjia and secured the chancellorship through that alliance.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，廢容管，隸嶺南西道，以供軍食，復以龔、像二州隸桂管。

translations.literal: Day yihai: Rong Circuit superintendency was abolished and placed under Western Lingnan Circuit to supply military provisions; Gong and Xiang Prefectures were again placed under Gui Circuit superintendency.
translations.idiomatic: On day yihai the Rong superintendency was abolished and absorbed into Western Lingnan to supply the armies; Gong and Xiang Prefectures were restored to Gui superintendency jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 戊子，以門下侍郎、同平章事杜審權同平章事，充鎮海節度使。

translations.literal: Day wuzi: Vice Director of the Chancellery and co–Director of the Chancellery Du Shenquan was made co–Director of the Chancellery and appointed military governor of Zhenhai.
translations.idiomatic: On day wuzi, Chancellery Vice Director and Co-Director Du Shenquan retained his chancellorship while being appointed military governor of Zhenhai.

sentences.zh: 六月，廢安南都護府，置行交州於海門鎮；

translations.literal: Sixth month: the Protectorate General of Annam was abolished, and a provisional Jiaozhou was established at Haimen garrison;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Protectorate General of Annam was abolished and a provisional Jiaozhou was set up at Haimen;

sentences.zh: 以右監門將軍宋戎為行交州刺史，以康承訓兼領安南及諸軍行營。

translations.literal: Right Gate Guard General Song Rong was made provisional prefect of Jiaozhou; Kang Cheng-xun was additionally put in charge of Annam and all military expeditionary camps.
translations.idiomatic: Right Gate Guard General Song Rong was made provisional governor of Jiaozhou, and Kang Cheng-xun was given concurrent command of Annam and all expeditionary forces.

sentences.zh: 閏月，以門下侍郎、同平章事杜悰同平章事，充鳳翔節度使；

translations.literal: In the intercalary month: Chancellery Vice Director and co–Director of the Chancellery Du Cong was made co–Director of the Chancellery and appointed military governor of Fengxiang;
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Chancellery Vice Director and Co-Director Du Cong retained his chancellorship while being made military governor of Fengxiang;

sentences.zh: 以兵部侍郎、判度支河南曹確同平章事。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of War and acting director of the Treasury Nan Cao Que was made co–Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of War and acting treasury director Nan Cao Que was made co-director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，辛卯朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, first day xinmao of the new moon: there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, on the first day of the new moon (day xinmao), there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 復置安南都護府於行交州，以宋戎為經略使；

translations.literal: The Protectorate General of Annam was reestablished at provisional Jiaozhou; Song Rong was made frontier commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: The Protectorate General of Annam was reestablished at provisional Jiaozhou, with Song Rong as frontier commissioner;

sentences.zh: 發山東兵萬人鎮之。

translations.literal: Ten thousand troops from Shandong were mobilized to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand troops from Shandong were deployed to garrison the post.

sentences.zh: 時諸道兵援安南者屯聚嶺南，江西、湖南饋運者皆溯湘江入澪渠、漓水，勞費艱澀，諸軍乏食。

translations.literal: At this time troops from the various circuits aiding Annam were massed in Lingnan; supply convoys from Jiangxi and Hunan all went up the Xiang River into the Ling Canal and Li River—laborious, costly, and difficult—and the armies lacked food.
translations.idiomatic: Troops from every circuit sent to relieve Annam were massed in Lingnan. Supplies from Jiangxi and Hunan had to go up the Xiang River and through the Ling and Li canals—an arduous route—and the armies went hungry.

sentences.zh: 潤州人陳磻石上言，請造千斛大舟，自福建運米泛海，不一月至廣州，從之，軍食以足。

translations.literal: Chen Pan of Run Prefecture submitted a memorial requesting that large ships of a thousand hu capacity be built to transport grain by sea from Fujian—not reaching Guangzhou in more than a month. The proposal was adopted, and military provisions were sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Pan of Runzhou proposed building thousand-hu grain ships to sail rice from Fujian to Guangzhou in under a month. The court approved, and the armies were fed.

sentences.zh: 然有司以和雇為名，奪商人舟，委其貨於岸側，舟入海或遇風濤沒溺，有司囚系綱吏、舟人，使償其米，人頗苦之。

translations.literal: However, the authorities under the name of hired transport seized merchants' boats, left their cargo on the shore, and when boats entering the sea encountered wind and waves and sank, the authorities imprisoned the rope handlers and boatmen and made them compensate for the grain—people suffered greatly from this.
translations.idiomatic: But officials, under the guise of hired transport, seized merchants' vessels and dumped their cargo ashore. When ships were lost in storms, the rope masters and sailors were imprisoned and forced to repay the lost grain—a burden people bitterly resented.

sentences.zh: 八月，嶺南東道節度使韋宙奏，蠻必向邕州，請分兵屯容、籐州。

translations.literal: Eighth month: Eastern Lingnan military governor Wei Zhou reported that the barbarians would surely head for Yong Prefecture and requested that troops be split to garrison Rong and Teng Prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Eastern Lingnan military governor Wei Zhou reported that the barbarians would surely strike at Yongzhou and asked that troops be posted at Rong and Teng.

sentences.zh: 夔王滋薨。

translations.literal: Prince of Kui Zi died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zi of Kui died.

sentences.zh: 敕以閣門使吳德應等為館驛使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Gate Officers Wu Deying and others as postal commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed imperial gate officers Wu Deying and others as postal commissioners.

sentences.zh: 台諫上言：故事，御史巡驛，不應忽以內臣代之。

translations.literal: Censorate remonstrators submitted: by precedent, censors inspected the post stations; eunuch officials should not suddenly be substituted in their place.
translations.idiomatic: Censors and remonstrators submitted that by precedent postal stations were inspected by censors—not suddenly replaced by inner-court eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 上諭以敕命已行，不可復改。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed that the edict had already been issued and could not be changed again.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied that the order had already been issued and could not be withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺劉蛻上言：「昔楚子縣陳，得申叔一言而復封之；

translations.literal: Left Reminder Liu Tui submitted: "In olden days when the ruler of Chu extinguished Chen, upon one word from Shen Shu he restored its fief;
translations.idiomatic: Left Reminder Liu Tui submitted: "When the ruler of Chu once annexed Chen, a single remonstrance from Shen Shu moved him to restore its independence;

sentences.zh: 太宗發卒修乾元殿，聞張玄素諫，即日罷之。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong dispatched laborers to repair the Qianyuan Hall; upon hearing Zhang Xuansu's remonstrance, he halted it that very day.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong had begun repairing the Qianyuan Hall, but when Zhang Xuansu remonstrated he stopped the work that very day.

sentences.zh: 自古明君所尚者，從諫如流，豈有已行而不改！

translations.literal: What enlightened rulers of old honored was heeding remonstrance as flowing water—how could there be something already done yet not changed!
translations.idiomatic: Enlightened rulers of old prized accepting remonstrance as readily as flowing water—how then can an order already issued remain unchanged!

sentences.zh: 且敕自陛下出之，自陛下改之，何為不可！」

translations.literal: Moreover, edicts issue from Your Majesty and are changed by Your Majesty—what could be impossible!"
translations.idiomatic: Edicts come from Your Majesty and may be revoked by Your Majesty—what is impossible about that!

sentences.zh: 弗聽。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 黠戛斯遣其臣合伊難支表求經籍及每年遣使走馬請歷，又欲討回鶻，使安西以來悉歸唐，不許。

translations.literal: Kirghiz sent their minister He Yinanzhi with a memorial requesting scriptures and each year dispatching envoys on horseback to request calendars; they also wished to campaign against the Uyghurs and restore everything west of Anxi to Tang—all was denied.
translations.idiomatic: Kirghiz sent the minister He Yinanzhi with a petition requesting Buddhist scriptures and annual calendar deliveries by courier, and proposing a campaign against the Uyghurs to restore Tang rule west of Anxi. The court refused.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲戌，以長安尉、集賢校理令狐滈為左拾遺。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day jiaxu: Chang'an District magistrate and Collation Scholar of the Hall of Assembled Worthies Linghu Hao was appointed Left Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on day jiaxu, Chang'an District Magistrate and Collation Scholar Linghu Hao was appointed Left Reminder.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，左拾遺劉蛻上言：「滈專家無子弟之法，布衣行公相之權。」

translations.literal: Day yihai: Left Reminder Liu Tui submitted: "Hao monopolized his house without the ways of a proper son, and as a commoner wielded the power of chancellor and minister."
translations.idiomatic: On day yihai, Left Reminder Liu Tui submitted: "Hao lorded over his household without the conduct of a dutiful son, and as a commoner wielded the power of chancellor and minister.

sentences.zh: 起居郎張雲言：「滈，父綯用李涿為安南，致南蠻至今為梗，由滈納賄，陷父於惡。」

translations.literal: Attendant Recorder Zhang Yun said: "Hao's father Tiao appointed Li Tuo to Annam, causing the southern barbarians to remain a thorn to this day—it was because Hao took bribes and drew his father into evil."
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Recorder Zhang Yun said: "Hao's father Linghu Tao appointed Li Tuo to Annam, and the southern barbarian threat that persists to this day owes to bribes Hao accepted, drawing his father into disgrace.

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁酉，雲復上言：「滈，父綯執政之時，人號『白衣宰相』。」

translations.literal: Eleventh month, day dingyou: Yun again submitted: "When Hao's father Tiao held office, people called him 'the chancellor in plain robes.'
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on day dingyou, Zhang Yun submitted again: "When Linghu Tao was in power, people called his son 'the chancellor in plain robes.'

sentences.zh: 滈亦上表引避，乃改詹事府司直。

translations.literal: Hao also submitted a memorial citing avoidance of conflict, and was thereupon changed to secretary-director in the Crown Prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: Hao himself submitted a memorial asking to withdraw, and was reassigned as secretary-director in the Crown Prince's household.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，廢宿泗觀察使，復以徐州為觀察府，以濠、泗隸焉。

translations.literal: Day xinsi: the Su-Si observation commission was abolished, and Xuzhou was again made an observation prefecture, with Hao and Si under its jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: On day xinsi the Su-Si observation commission was abolished; Xuzhou was restored as an observation prefecture with Haozhou and Sizhou under its jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 十二月，南詔寇西川。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Nanzhao raided West Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Nanzhao invaded western Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 昭義節度使沈詢奴歸秦，與詢侍婢通，詢欲殺之，未果。

translations.literal: Zhaoyi military governor Shen Xun's slave Guiqin had relations with Xun's maidservant; Xun wished to kill him but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyi military governor Shen Xun's slave Guiqin had an affair with one of Xun's maidservants. Xun tried to have him killed but failed.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，歸秦結牙將作亂，攻府第，殺詢。

translations.literal: Day yiyou: Guiqin joined with guard officers to rebel, attacked the headquarters residence, and killed Xun.
translations.idiomatic: On day yiyou, Guiqin incited guard officers to mutiny, stormed the headquarters, and killed Shen Xun.

sentences.zh: 懿宗昭聖恭惠孝皇帝上咸通五年（

translations.literal: Above: Emperor Yizong, the Sagely, Respectful, and Gracious Filial Emperor; fifth year of Xiantong (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yizong, the Sagely, Respectful, and Gracious Filial Emperor; fifth year of Xiantong (

sentences.zh: 甲申，公元八六四年）

translations.literal: jiashen, AD 864)
translations.idiomatic: jiashen, AD 864)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，以京兆尹李蠙為昭義節度使，取歸秦心肝以祭沈詢。

translations.literal: Spring, first month: Capital Metropolitan Prefect Li Fan was appointed Zhaoyi military governor; Guiqin's heart and liver were taken to sacrifice to Shen Xun.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, Capital Metropolitan Prefect Li Fan was appointed Zhaoyi military governor and had Guiqin's heart and liver torn out to sacrifice to Shen Xun.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使令狐綯為其子滈訟冤。

translations.literal: Huainan military governor Linghu Tao pleaded his son Hao's innocence.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan military governor Linghu Tao petitioned on behalf of his son Hao, claiming injustice.

sentences.zh: 貶張雲興元少尹，劉蛻華陰令，赦曰：「雖嘉蹇諤之忠，難逃疏易之責。」

translations.literal: Zhang Yun was demoted to vice prefect of Xingyuan, Liu Tui to magistrate of Huayin; the amnesty stated: "Although we commend the forthright loyalty of blunt remonstrance, one cannot escape the blame of careless levity."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yun was demoted to vice prefect of Xingyuan and Liu Tui to magistrate of Huayin. The amnesty read: "Though we commend their blunt loyalty, they cannot escape blame for reckless levity."

sentences.zh: 丙午，西川奏，南詔寇巂州，刺史喻士珍破之，獲千餘人。

translations.literal: Day bingwu: West Sichuan reported that Nanzhao raided Xizhou; Prefect Yu Shizhen defeated them and captured more than a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: On day bingwu, western Sichuan reported a Nanzhao raid on Xizhou. Prefect Yu Shizhen repulsed them and took more than a thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 詔發右神策兵五千及諸道兵戍之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered five thousand Right Shence troops and troops from various circuits to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict mobilized five thousand Right Shence troops and forces from other circuits to reinforce the frontier.

sentences.zh: 忠武大將顏慶復請築新安、遏戎二城，從之。

translations.literal: Zhongwu commander-in-chief Yan Qingfu requested building the two fortresses of Xin'an and E'rong; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu commander Yan Qingfu proposed building fortresses at Xin'an and E'rong, and the court approved.

sentences.zh: 以容管經略使張茵兼句當交州事。

translations.literal: Rong Circuit frontier commissioner Zhang Yin was additionally put in charge of Jiaozhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Rong frontier commissioner Zhang Yin was given concurrent charge of Jiaozhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 益海門鎮兵滿二萬五千人，令茵進取安南。

translations.literal: Haimen garrison troops were increased to twenty-five thousand; Zhang Yin was ordered to advance and recover Annam.
translations.idiomatic: Haimen garrison strength was raised to twenty-five thousand, and Zhang Yin was ordered to advance and recover Annam.

sentences.zh: 二月，己巳，以刑部尚書、鹽鐵轉運使李福同平章事、充西川節度使。

translations.literal: Second month, day jisi: Minister of Justice and salt and iron transport commissioner Li Fu was made co–Director of the Chancellery and appointed military governor of West Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on day jisi, Minister of Justice and salt-and-iron transport commissioner Li Fu was made co-director of the Chancellery and military governor of western Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 甲申，前西川節度使蕭鄴左遷山南西道觀察使。

translations.literal: Day jiashen: former West Sichuan military governor Xiao Ye was demoted to observation commissioner of South Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On day jiashen former western Sichuan military governor Xiao Ye was demoted to observation commissioner of South Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 三月，丁酉，彗星出於婁，長三尺。

translations.literal: Third month, day dingyou: a comet appeared in the constellation Lou, three feet in length.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on day dingyou, a comet three feet long appeared in the constellation Lou.

sentences.zh: 己亥，司天監奏：「按《星經》，是名含譽，瑞星也。」

translations.literal: Day jihai: the Directorate of Astronomy reported: "According to the Classic of Stars, it is called Hanyu, an auspicious star."
translations.idiomatic: On day jihai the Directorate of Astronomy reported: "According to the Classic of Stars, this is Hanyu—an auspicious star.

sentences.zh: 上主大喜。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 請宣示中外，編諸史策。」

translations.literal: They requested that it be proclaimed within and without the court and recorded in the historical annals."
translations.idiomatic: The astronomers asked that it be announced throughout the empire and entered in the dynastic annals.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was granted.

sentences.zh: 康承訓至邕州，蠻寇益熾，詔發許、滑、青、汴、兗、鄆、宣、潤八道兵以授之。

translations.literal: Kang Cheng-xun reached Yong Prefecture; barbarian raids grew fiercer. An edict mobilized troops from the eight circuits of Xu, Hua, Qing, Bian, Yan, Yun, Xuan, and Run and entrusted them to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Kang Cheng-xun reached Yongzhou, barbarian raids intensified. An edict mobilized troops from Xu, Hua, Qing, Bian, Yan, Yun, Xuan, and Run and placed them under his command.

sentences.zh: 承訓不設斥候，南詔帥群蠻近六萬寇邕州，將入境，承訓乃遣六道兵凡萬人拒之，以獠為導，紿之。

translations.literal: Cheng-xun did not set out scouts. Nanzhao led a horde of nearly sixty thousand barbarians against Yong Prefecture. About to enter the border, Cheng-xun then dispatched troops from six circuits totaling ten thousand to resist, using tribal guides who deceived them.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng-xun posted no scouts. Nanzhao led nearly sixty thousand barbarians against Yongzhou. As they were about to cross the border, Cheng-xun sent ten thousand men from six circuits to meet them, guided by tribal auxiliaries who betrayed them.

sentences.zh: 敵至，不設備，五道兵八千人皆沒，惟天平軍後一日至，得免。

translations.literal: When the enemy arrived, they were unprepared; eight thousand troops from five circuits were all lost. Only the Tianping Army, arriving one day later, escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy struck without warning. Eight thousand men from five circuits were wiped out. Only the Tianping contingent, arriving a day late, escaped.

sentences.zh: 承訓聞之，惶怖不知所為。

translations.literal: When Cheng-xun heard of it, he was terrified and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng-xun was terrified and at a loss when he heard the news.

sentences.zh: 節度副使李行素帥眾治壕柵，甫畢，蠻軍已合圍。

translations.literal: Vice military governor Li Xingsu led the troops in digging moats and building palisades; just as they finished, the barbarian army had already encircled them.
translations.idiomatic: Vice military governor Li Xingsu led the men in digging trenches and raising palisades—but barely had they finished when the barbarian army closed around the city.

sentences.zh: 留四日，治攻具，將就，諸將請夜分道斫蠻營，承訓不許，有天平小校再三力爭，乃許之。

translations.literal: They remained four days while siege equipment was prepared; just as it was nearly ready, the generals requested a night raid in separate columns to strike the barbarian camp. Cheng-xun would not agree; a Tianping junior officer argued forcefully again and again, and only then was it permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians besieged the city for four days while preparing siege engines. As the assault was about to begin, the generals asked to launch a night raid on the enemy camps in separate columns. Cheng-xun refused—until a Tianping junior officer argued him down again and again and he relented.

sentences.zh: 小校將勇士三百，夜，縋而出，散燒蠻營，斬首五百餘級。

translations.literal: The junior officer led three hundred brave warriors; by night they were lowered by rope to get out, scattered to burn barbarian camps, and beheaded more than five hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The junior officer led three hundred picked men. By night they were lowered over the walls, set fire to the enemy camps in several places, and took more than five hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 蠻大驚，間一日，解圍去。

translations.literal: The barbarians were greatly alarmed; after one day they lifted the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians were thrown into panic; a day later they broke off the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 承訓乃遣諸軍數千追之，所殺虜不滿三百級，皆溪獠脅從者。

translations.literal: Cheng-xun then sent several thousand from the various armies in pursuit; those killed and captured amounted to fewer than three hundred—all were stream-dwelling tribesmen forced to follow along.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng-xun then sent several thousand men in pursuit, but they killed and captured fewer than three hundred—mostly coerced tribal levies.

sentences.zh: 承訓騰奏告捷，雲大破蠻賊，中外皆賀。

translations.literal: Cheng-xun submitted an urgent memorial announcing victory, claiming a great defeat of the barbarian bandits; within and without the court all congratulated.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng-xun sent an urgent victory report claiming a crushing defeat of the barbarians, and congratulations poured in from across the empire.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，以兵部侍郎、判戶部蕭置同平章事。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Vice Minister of War and acting director of the Household Bureau Xiao Zhi was made co–Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, Vice Minister of War and acting household director Xiao Zhi was made co-director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 置，復之孫也。

translations.literal: Zhi was the grandson of Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Zhi was the grandson of Xiao Fu.

sentences.zh: 加康承訓檢校右僕射，賞破蠻之功也。

translations.literal: Kang Cheng-xun was promoted to honorary Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat, in reward for defeating the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Cheng-xun was given the honorary title of Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat in reward for his supposed victory over the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 自餘奏功受賞者，皆承訓子弟親暱，燒營將校不遷一級，由是軍中怨怒，聲流道路。

translations.literal: Of the rest who submitted claims of merit and received rewards, all were Cheng-xun's sons, younger brothers, and close associates; the officer who burned the camp was not promoted a single grade—therefore resentment and anger spread through the army, and the story traveled along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: All other rewards went to Cheng-xun's sons, brothers, and cronies—not one promotion for the officer who had burned the enemy camps. Resentment spread through the ranks and outrage traveled the highways.

sentences.zh: 五月，敕：「徐州土風雄勁，甲士精強，比因罷節，頗多逃匿，宜令徐泗團練使選募軍士三千人赴邕州防戍，待嶺外事寧，即與代歸。」

translations.literal: Fifth month, edict: "The character of Xuzhou's land is fierce and strong, and its armored soldiers are elite. Recently, because the military commission was abolished, many have fled and hidden themselves. The Xu-Si defense commissioner should be ordered to select and recruit three thousand soldiers to go garrison Yong Prefecture; when affairs beyond the Ling are settled, they shall be replaced and return."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month an edict read: "Xuzhou's warriors are fierce and its soldiers skilled. Since the military commission was abolished many have gone into hiding. The Xu-Si defense commissioner shall recruit three thousand men for garrison duty at Yongzhou; when Lingnan is pacified they shall be relieved and sent home."

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，西川奏兩林鬼主邀南詔蠻，敗之，殺獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: West Sichuan reported that the Two Forests Ghost Lord intercepted Nanzhao barbarians, defeated them, and killed and captured a great many.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, western Sichuan reported that the Two Forests Ghost Lord had ambushed Nanzhao forces, defeated them, and inflicted heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 保塞城使杜守連不從南詔，帥眾詣黎州降。

translations.literal: Baosai fort commander Du Shoulian would not follow Nanzhao, led the masses to Lizhou, and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Du Shoulian, commander of Baosai Fort, refused to submit to Nanzhao, led his troops to Lizhou, and surrendered to Tang.

sentences.zh: 嶺南東道節度使韋宙具知康承訓所為，以書白宰相。

translations.literal: Lingnan East Circuit military governor Wei Zhou fully knew what Kang Cheng-xun had done, and by letter informed the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhou, military governor of Lingnan East Circuit, knew exactly what Kang Cheng-xun had been up to and wrote to the chief ministers to expose him.

sentences.zh: 承訓亦自疑懼，累表辭疾，乃以承訓為右武衛大將軍、分司，以容管經略使張茵為嶺南西道節度使，復以容管四州別為經略使。

translations.literal: Cheng-xun also grew fearful and suspicious himself, repeatedly submitting memorials to resign on grounds of illness. Thereupon Cheng-xun was made Grand General of the Right Guard with a sinecure post; Rongguan frontier commissioner Zhang Yin was made military governor of Lingnan West Circuit, and the four prefectures of Rongguan were again made a separate frontier commission.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng-xun himself grew anxious and repeatedly asked to resign on grounds of illness. The court made him Grand General of the Right Guard with a nominal post, replaced him with Rongguan frontier commissioner Zhang Yin as military governor of Lingnan West Circuit, and restored the four Rongguan prefectures as a separate frontier command.

sentences.zh: 時南詔知邕州空竭，不復入寇，茵久之不敢進軍取安南。

translations.literal: At this time Nanzhao knew Yong Prefecture was empty and exhausted, and no longer invaded; Yin for a long time did not dare advance his army to recover Annam.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao, seeing that Yongzhou was drained of men and supplies, stopped raiding; Zhang Yin for a long time did not dare march south to retake Annam.

sentences.zh: 夏侯孜薦驍衛將軍高駢代之，乃以駢為安南都護、本管經略招討使，茵所將兵悉以授之。

translations.literal: Xia Hou Zi recommended General of the Brave Guard Gao Pian to replace him. Thereupon Pian was made Protector-General of Annam and frontier punitive commissioner for his circuit; all the troops Yin had commanded were turned over to him.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Hou Zi recommended General of the Brave Guard Gao Pian for the post. Pian was appointed Protector-General of Annam and frontier punitive commissioner, and every soldier under Zhang Yin was transferred to his command.

sentences.zh: 駢，崇文之孫也，世在禁軍。

translations.literal: Pian was the grandson of Chongwen; for generations his family served in the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian was the grandson of Gao Chongwen and came from a family that had served for generations in the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 駢頗讀書，好談今古，兩軍宦官多譽之，累廷右神策都虞候；

translations.literal: Pian was quite well read, fond of discussing past and present; eunuchs of both armies often praised him, and he was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander of the Right Divine Strategy Army;
translations.idiomatic: Pian was well read and loved to hold forth on history; eunuchs of both palace armies spoke highly of him, and he rose repeatedly to deputy commander of the Right Divine Strategy Army;

sentences.zh: 党項叛，將禁兵萬人戍長武，屢有功，遷秦州防禦使，復有功，故委以安南。

translations.literal: When the Tangut rebelled, he led ten thousand Palace Guard troops to garrison Changwu, achieved repeated merit, was transferred to defense commissioner of Qin Prefecture, achieved merit again, and therefore was entrusted with Annam.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tangut rebelled he took ten thousand palace troops to garrison Changwu and won repeated victories; promoted to defense commissioner of Qin Prefecture, he distinguished himself again, and so the court entrusted him with Annam.

sentences.zh: 冬，十一月，以門下侍郎、同平章事夏侯孜同平章事，充河東節度使。

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month: Vice Director of the Chancellery and co-director of the Chancellery Xia Hou Zi, retaining his co-chancellorship, was appointed military governor of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of winter, Vice Director of the Chancellery and co-director Xia Hou Zi kept his seat on the council and was also appointed military governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以翰林學士承旨、兵部侍郎路巖同平章事，時年三十六。

translations.literal: On renyin, Hanlin Academician-in-Waiting and Vice Minister of War Lu Yan was made co-director of the Chancellery; he was thirty-six years old at the time.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renyin, Hanlin Academician-in-Waiting and Vice Minister of War Lu Yan was made co-director of the Chancellery at the age of thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 懿宗昭聖恭惠孝皇帝上咸通六年（

translations.literal: Above: Emperor Yizong, the Sagely, Respectful, and Gracious Filial Emperor; sixth year of Xiantong (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yizong, the Sagely, Respectful, and Gracious Filial Emperor; sixth year of Xiantong (

sentences.zh: 乙酉，公元八六五年）

translations.literal: yiyou, AD 865)
translations.idiomatic: yiyou, AD 865)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，丁已，始以懿安皇后配饗憲宗室。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on dingsi: for the first time Empress Yi'an was paired in sacrifice in Emperor Xianzong's ancestral shrine.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, on the day dingsi, Empress Yi'an was for the first time given paired offerings in Emperor Xianzong's ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 時王皞復為禮院檢討官，更申前議，朝廷竟從之。

translations.literal: At this time Wang Hao again served as review officer of the Board of Rites, restated his earlier proposal, and the court ultimately agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hao, once again serving as a review officer in the Board of Rites, renewed his earlier proposal, and the court at last accepted it.

sentences.zh: 諸道進私白者，閩中為多，故宦官多閩人。

translations.literal: Of those who presented private white silks from the various circuits, Fujian supplied the most; therefore many eunuchs were men from Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Of the tribute of private white silk sent up from the provinces, Fujian contributed the most— which is why so many eunuchs were Fujianese.

sentences.zh: 福建觀察使杜宣猷每寒食遣吏分祭其先□，宦官德之，庚申，以宣猷為宣歙觀察使，時人謂之「敕使墓戶」。

translations.literal: Fujian observation commissioner Du Xuanyou every Cold Food Festival sent clerks in separate groups to sacrifice at their ancestors' graves; eunuchs were grateful to him. On gengshen he was made Xuanshe observation commissioner; people of the time called him "the edict-envoy's grave-keeper."
translations.idiomatic: Every Cold Food Festival, Fujian observation commissioner Du Xuanyou sent out clerks to tend the ancestral graves of eunuchs' families. The eunuchs were deeply obliged. On gengshen he was promoted to Xuanshe observation commissioner, and contemporaries nicknamed him "the edict-envoy's grave-keeper."

sentences.zh: 三月，中書侍郎、同平章事蕭置薨。

translations.literal: Third month: Vice Director of the Secretariat and co-director of the Chancellery Xiao Zhi died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Vice Director of the Secretariat and co-director Xiao Zhi died.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，以前東川節度使高璩為兵部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: former Dongchuan military governor Gao Chu was made Vice Minister of War and co-director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, former Dongchuan military governor Gao Chu was appointed Vice Minister of War and co-director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 璩，元裕之子也。

translations.literal: Chu was the son of Yuanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Chu was the son of Gao Yuanyu.

sentences.zh: 楊收建議，以「蠻寇積年未平，兩河兵戍嶺南冒瘴霧物故者什六七，請於江西積粟，募強弩三萬人，以應接嶺南，道近便，仍建節以重其權。」

translations.literal: Yang Shou proposed: "The barbarian raids have gone unresolved for years. Of the soldiers from the two He regions garrisoning Lingnan who have suffered miasma and disease, six or seven in ten have died. I request storing grain in Jiangxi and recruiting thirty thousand crossbowmen to support Lingnan—the route is nearer and more convenient, and a military commission should still be established to weight its authority."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shou proposed: "The barbarian raids have dragged on for years. Of the troops from the two He regions sent to garrison Lingnan, six or seven in ten have perished from miasma and disease. I ask that grain be stockpiled in Jiangxi and thirty thousand crossbowmen recruited to reinforce Lingnan—the route is shorter and easier, and a military commission should be established to give the command full authority."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 五月，辛丑，置鎮南軍於洪州。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on xinchou: the Zhennan Army was established at Hong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the day xinchou, the Zhennan Army was established at Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 巂州刺史喻士珍貪獪，掠兩林蠻以易金。

translations.literal: Prefect Yu Shizhen of Xi Prefecture was greedy and cunning; he plundered the Two Forests tribesmen to exchange them for gold.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shizhen, prefect of Xi Prefecture, was greedy and ruthless; he seized tribesmen of the Two Forests and sold them for gold.

sentences.zh: 南詔復寇巂州，兩林蠻開門納之，南詔盡殺戍卒，士珍降之。

translations.literal: Nanzhao again raided Xi Prefecture; the Two Forests tribesmen opened the gates and admitted them; Nanzhao killed all the garrison troops, and Shizhen surrendered to them.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao attacked Xi Prefecture again. The Two Forests tribes opened the gates to them; Nanzhao slaughtered the entire garrison, and Shizhen surrendered.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，以桂管觀察使嚴譔為鎮南節度使。

translations.literal: On renyin, Gui Circuit observation commissioner Yan Zuan was made military governor of Zhennan.
translations.idiomatic: On the day renyin, Gui Circuit observation commissioner Yan Zuan was appointed military governor of Zhennan.

sentences.zh: 譔，震之從孫也

translations.literal: Zuan was the grandnephew of Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zuan was the grandnephew of Yan Zhen.

sentences.zh: 六月，高璩薨。

translations.literal: Sixth month: Gao Chu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Gao Chu died.

sentences.zh: 以御史大夫徐商為兵部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Xu Shang was made Vice Minister of War and co-director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Xu Shang was appointed Vice Minister of War and co-director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，立皇子侃為郢王，儼為普王。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: the princes Kan and Yan were established as Prince of Ying and Prince of Pu respectively.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, the princes Kan and Yan were enfeoffed as Prince of Ying and Prince of Pu.

sentences.zh: 高駢治兵於海門，未進。

translations.literal: Gao Pian drilled troops at Haimen but did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian trained his army at Haimen but did not march forward.

sentences.zh: 監軍李維周惡駢，欲去之，屢趣駢使進軍。

translations.literal: Army supervisor Li Weizhou hated Pian and wanted to remove him; he repeatedly pressed Pian to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Army supervisor Li Weizhou despised Pian and wanted him gone; he kept pressing Pian to advance.

sentences.zh: 駢以五千人先濟，約維周發兵應援。

translations.literal: Pian crossed first with five thousand men, arranging for Weizhou to mobilize troops in support.
translations.idiomatic: Pian crossed ahead with five thousand men, with Weizhou pledged to follow with reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 駢既行，維周擁餘眾，不發一卒以繼之。

translations.literal: Once Pian had departed, Weizhou held the remaining forces and did not send a single soldier to follow.
translations.idiomatic: After Pian had gone, Weizhou kept the rest of the army and did not send a single man after him.

sentences.zh: 九月，駢至南定，峰州蠻眾近五萬，方獲田，駢掩擊，大破之，收其所獲以食軍。

translations.literal: Ninth month: Pian reached Nanding; the Feng Prefecture tribesmen numbered nearly fifty thousand and were harvesting fields; Pian launched a surprise attack, routed them thoroughly, and took their harvest to feed his army.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Pian reached Nanding. Nearly fifty thousand Fengzhou tribesmen were out harvesting their fields; Pian struck by surprise, crushed them, and used their grain to feed his troops.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，壬子，太皇太后鄭氏崩。

translations.literal: Winter, twelfth month, on renzi: Grand Empress Dowager Lady Zheng died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of winter, on the day renzi, Grand Empress Dowager Lady Zheng died.

sentences.zh: 懿宗昭聖恭惠孝皇帝上咸通七年（

translations.literal: Above: Emperor Yizong, the Sagely, Respectful, and Gracious Filial Emperor; seventh year of Xiantong (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yizong, the Sagely, Respectful, and Gracious Filial Emperor; seventh year of Xiantong (

sentences.zh: 丙戌，公元八六六年）

translations.literal: bingxu, AD 866)
translations.idiomatic: bingxu, AD 866)

sentences.zh: 春，二月，歸義節度使張義潮奏北庭回鶻固俊克西州、北庭、輪台、清鎮等城。

translations.literal: Spring, second month: Guiyi military governor Zhang Yichao reported that the Beiting Uyghur Guo Jun had captured Xizhou, Beiting, Luntai, Qingzhen, and other cities.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring, Guiyi military governor Zhang Yichao reported that the Beiting Uyghur Guo Jun had recaptured Xizhou, Beiting, Luntai, Qingzhen, and other towns.

sentences.zh: 論恐熱寓居廓州，糾合旁側諸部，欲為邊患，皆不從。

translations.literal: Lun Kongre took refuge in Kuo Prefecture, gathered the neighboring tribes, and wished to make trouble on the frontier, but none obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Lun Kongre, living in exile at Kuozhou, tried to rally the neighboring tribes to raid the frontier, but none would follow him.

sentences.zh: 所向盡為仇敵，無所容。

translations.literal: Wherever he turned, all became enemies; he had nowhere to stay.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere he turned he found enemies; he had nowhere left to go.

sentences.zh: 仇人認告拓跋懷光於鄯州，懷光引兵擊破之。

translations.literal: An enemy denounced him to Tuoba Huailiang at Zha Prefecture; Huailiang led troops and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: A foe denounced him to Tuoba Huailiang at Zhaozhou; Huailiang marched out and routed him.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊寅，以河東節度使劉潼為西川節度使。

translations.literal: Third month, on wuyin: Hedong military governor Liu Tong was made military governor of West Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on the day wuyin, Hedong military governor Liu Tong was appointed military governor of West Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 初，南詔圍巂州，東蠻浪稽部竭力助之，遂屠其城，卑籠部怨南詔殺其父兄，導忠武戍兵襲浪稽，滅之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Nanzhao besieged Xi Prefecture, the Eastern Barbarian Langji tribe had assisted with all its strength and sacked the city. The Bilong tribe resented Nanzhao for killing their fathers and elder brothers and guided Zhongwu garrison troops in a raid on the Langji, destroying them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Nanzhao besieged Xi Prefecture, the Eastern Barbarian Langji tribe had fought hard on Nanzhao's side and helped sack the city. The Bilong tribe, furious that Nanzhao had killed their fathers and brothers, guided Zhongwu garrison troops in a strike on the Langji and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 南詔由是怨唐。

translations.literal: Nanzhao therefore bore resentment toward Tang.
translations.idiomatic: From this Nanzhao turned against Tang.

sentences.zh: 南詔遣清平官董成等詣成都，節度使李福盛儀衛以見之。

translations.literal: Nanzhao sent Chief Minister Dong Cheng and others to Chengdu; military governor Li Fu displayed full ceremonial guard to receive them.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao sent its chief minister Dong Cheng and others to Chengdu; military governor Li Fu received them with full ceremonial display.

sentences.zh: 故事，南詔使見節度使，拜伏於庭，成等曰：「驃信已應天順人，我見節度使當抗禮。」

translations.literal: By precedent, when Nanzhao envoys met the military governor they bowed prostrate in the courtyard. Cheng and the others said: "The Piluo has answered Heaven and conformed to the people's will; when we meet the military governor we should receive each other as equals."
translations.idiomatic: By custom, Nanzhao envoys prostrated themselves in the courtyard before the military governor. Cheng and his party said: "Our Piluo has received Heaven's mandate and won the people's assent; when we meet the military governor we should greet each other as equals."

sentences.zh: 傳言往返，自旦至日中不決。

translations.literal: Messages went back and forth from dawn until noon without resolution.
translations.idiomatic: Messages shuttled back and forth from dawn until midday with no agreement.

sentences.zh: 將士皆憤怒，福乃命捽而毆之，因械繫於獄。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers were all furious; Fu then ordered them seized and beaten, and shackled and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers were outraged; Fu had the envoys seized and beaten, then shackled and thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 劉潼到鎮，釋之，奏遣還國。

translations.literal: When Liu Tong reached his post, he released them and memorialized to send them back to their country.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Tong took up his post he freed them and memorialized that they be sent home.

sentences.zh: 詔召成等至京師，見於別殿，厚賜，勞而遣之。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Cheng and the others to the capital; they were received in a side hall, generously rewarded, comforted, and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned Cheng and his party to the capital; they were received in a side hall, richly rewarded, treated with courtesy, and sent on their way.

sentences.zh: 成德節度使王紹懿，在鎮十年，為政寬簡，軍民便之。

translations.literal: Chengde military governor Wang Shaoyi had been at his post ten years; his government was lenient and simple, and army and people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shaoyi had governed Chengde for ten years with a light and straightforward hand, to the satisfaction of soldiers and civilians alike.

sentences.zh: 疾病，召兄紹鼎之子都知兵馬使景崇而告之曰：「吾兄以汝之幼，以軍政授我。

translations.literal: When ill, he summoned his brother Shaoding's son, commander of military affairs Jingchong, and told him: "My elder brother, because you were young, entrusted military affairs to me.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill he summoned his brother Shaoding's son Jingchong, commander of military affairs, and said: "My brother, seeing how young you were, entrusted the army and government to me.

sentences.zh: 汝今長矣，我復以軍政歸汝。

translations.literal: You are grown now; I return military affairs to you.
translations.idiomatic: You are a man now; I give the army and government back to you.

sentences.zh: 努力為之，上忠朝廷，下和鄰籓，勿墜吾兄之業，汝之功也。」

translations.literal: Strive at it—loyal above to the court, harmonious below with neighboring circuits; do not let my brother's enterprise fall—that will be your achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Do your utmost: loyal to the throne above, at peace with neighboring circuits below. Do not let my brother's legacy slip—that will be your merit."

sentences.zh: 言竟而薨。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking, he died.
translations.idiomatic: With those words he died.

sentences.zh: 閏月，吐蕃寇邠寧，節度使薛弘宗拒卻之。

translations.literal: Intercalary month: Tibet raided Binning; military governor Xue Hongzong repulsed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Tibet raided Binning; military governor Xue Hongzong drove them back.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛巳，貶前西川節度使李福為蘄王傅。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, on xinsi: former West Sichuan military governor Li Fu was demoted to tutor of the Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the day xinsi, former West Sichuan military governor Li Fu was demoted to tutor of the Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 五月，葬孝明皇后於景陵之側，主祔別廟。

translations.literal: Fifth month: Empress Xiaoming was buried beside Jingling; her tablet was enshrined in a separate temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Empress Xiaoming was buried beside Jingling, with her spirit tablet placed in a separate shrine.

sentences.zh: 六月，魏博節度使何弘敬薨，軍中立其子左司馬全皞為留後。

translations.literal: Sixth month: Weibo military governor He Hongjing died; the army established his son, Left Vice Cavalry General Quanhao, as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Weibo military governor He Hongjing died; the army installed his son, Left Vice Cavalry General He Quanhao, as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 以王景崇為成德留後。
