translations.literal: Wang Jingchong was made acting governor of Chengde.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingchong was appointed acting governor of Chengde.

sentences.zh: 南詔酋龍遣善闡節度使楊緝思助安南節度使段酋遷守交趾，以范暱些為安南都統，趙諾眉為扶邪都統。

translations.literal: Nanzhao chieftain Long sent Shanchan military governor Yang Jisi to assist Annam military governor Duan Qiouqian in holding Jiaozhi; Fan Nixie was made overall commander of Annam, Zhao Nuomei made overall commander of Fuye.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao chieftain Long sent Shanchan military governor Yang Jisi to help Annam military governor Duan Qiouqian hold Jiaozhi; Fan Nixie was made overall commander of Annam and Zhao Nuomei overall commander of Fuye.

sentences.zh: 監陳敕使韋仲宰將七千人至峰州，高駢得以益其軍，進擊南詔，屢破之。

translations.literal: Supervising envoy Wei Zhongzai of the Chen edict mission led seven thousand men to Feng Prefecture; Gao Pian was thus able to augment his army, advance against Nanzhao, and repeatedly defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising envoy Wei Zhongzai of the Chen mission arrived at Fengzhou with seven thousand men; Gao Pian was able to reinforce his army, push against Nanzhao, and win victory after victory.

sentences.zh: 捷奏至海門，李維周皆匿之，數月無聲問。

translations.literal: Victory reports reaching Haimen were all suppressed by Li Weizhou; for months there was no word.
translations.idiomatic: Victory reports reaching Haimen were all suppressed by Li Weizhou; for months the court heard nothing.

sentences.zh: 上怪之，以問維周，維周奏駢駐軍峰州，玩寇不進。

translations.literal: The emperor found this strange and questioned Weizhou; Weizhou memorialized that Pian was encamped at Feng Prefecture, toying with the enemy and not advancing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was puzzled and questioned Weizhou, who reported that Pian was sitting at Fengzhou, dallying with the enemy and refusing to advance.

sentences.zh: 上怒，以右武衛將軍王晏權代駢鎮安南，召駢詣闕，欲重貶之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry; Right Guard General Wang Yanquan was sent to replace Pian as governor of Annam, and Pian was summoned to court for heavy demotion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious. Right Guard General Wang Yanquan was sent to replace Pian in Annam, and Pian was recalled to court for severe punishment.

sentences.zh: 晏權，智興之從子也。

translations.literal: Yanquan was the nephew of Zhixing.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanquan was the nephew of Wang Zhixing.

sentences.zh: 是月，駢大破南詔蠻於交趾，殺獲甚眾，遂圍交趾城。

translations.literal: That same month, Pian thoroughly defeated Nanzhao barbarians at Jiaozhi, killing and capturing a great many, and then besieged Jiaozhi city.
translations.idiomatic: That same month Pian routed the Nanzhao forces at Jiaozhi with heavy slaughter and capture, then laid siege to the city.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，以何全皞為魏博留後。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: He Quanhao was made acting governor of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn, He Quanhao was confirmed as acting governor of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲申，以門下侍郎、同平章事楊收為宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on jiashen: Vice Director of the Chancellery and co-director Yang Shou was made Xuanshe observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the day jiashen, Vice Director of the Chancellery and co-director Yang Shou was transferred out to serve as Xuanshe observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 收性侈靡，門吏僮奴多倚為奸利。

translations.literal: Shou's character was extravagant; gate clerks and servant boys often relied on him for illicit profit.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shou lived lavishly, and his gate clerks and household servants used his name to turn a dishonest profit.

sentences.zh: 楊玄價兄弟受方鎮之賂，屢有請托，收不能盡從。

translations.literal: Yang Xuanjia and his brothers accepted bribes from regional commanders and repeatedly made requests; Shou could not grant them all.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuanjia and his brothers took bribes from regional commanders and kept asking favors; Shou could not satisfy every request.

sentences.zh: 玄價怒，以為叛己，故出之。

translations.literal: Xuanjia was enraged, believing himself betrayed, and therefore had him transferred out.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanjia, furious at what he took for betrayal, arranged to have him removed from court.

sentences.zh: 拓跋懷光以五百騎入廓州，生擒論恐熱，先刖其足，數而斬之，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Tuoba Huailiang entered Kuo Prefecture with five hundred cavalry, captured Lun Kongre alive, first cut off his feet, rebuked and beheaded him, and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Huailiang rode into Kuozhou with five hundred cavalry, took Lun Kongre alive, cut off his feet, denounced and beheaded him, and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 其部眾東奔秦州，尚延心邀擊，破之，悉奏遷於嶺南。

translations.literal: His followers fled east toward Qin Prefecture; Shang Yanxin intercepted and defeated them, and memorialized to relocate them all to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: His followers fled east toward Qinzhou; Shang Yanxin cut them off, defeated them, and memorialized to resettle the whole band in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃由是衰絕，乞離胡君臣不知所終。

translations.literal: Tibet thus fell into utter decline; the whereabouts of the Qilihu ruler and ministers became unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet collapsed from this blow; the Qilihu king and his ministers vanished without trace.

sentences.zh: 高駢圍交趾十餘日，蠻困蹙甚，城且下，會得王晏權牒，已與李維周將大軍發海門。

translations.literal: Gao Pian besieged Jiaozhi for more than ten days; the barbarians were severely pressed and the city was about to fall when word came of Wang Yanquan's dispatch—that he and Li Weizhou were leading a great army from Haimen.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Pian had besieged Jiaozhi for more than ten days; the enemy was hard pressed and the city was on the verge of surrender when he learned from Wang Yanquan's dispatch that Yanquan and Li Weizhou were marching a large force from Haimen.

sentences.zh: 駢即以軍事授韋仲宰，與麾下百餘人北歸。

translations.literal: Pian immediately entrusted military affairs to Wei Zhongzai and returned north with a little over a hundred followers.
translations.idiomatic: Pian immediately turned command over to Wei Zhongzai and rode north with a little over a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 先是，仲宰遣小使王惠贊，駢遣小校曾袞入告交趾之捷。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhongzai had sent junior envoy Wang Huizan and Pian had sent junior officer Zeng Gun to report the victory at Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhongzai had sent junior envoy Wang Huizan and Pian had sent junior officer Zeng Gun to carry word of the victory at Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 至海中，望見旌旗東來，問遊船，雲新經略使與監軍也。

translations.literal: At sea they saw banners coming from the east; asking passing boats, they were told it was the new frontier commissioner and the army supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Out at sea they saw banners approaching from the east; asking passing boats, they learned it was the new frontier commissioner and the army supervisor.

sentences.zh: 二人謀曰：「維周必奪表留我。」

translations.literal: The two men plotted: "Weizhou will surely seize our memorials and detain us."
translations.idiomatic: The two men agreed: "Weizhou is sure to seize our reports and hold us."

sentences.zh: 乃匿於島間，維周過，即馳詣京師。

translations.literal: So they hid among the islands; once Weizhou had passed, they raced to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: So they hid among the islands; after Weizhou had passed they raced straight to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上得奏，大喜，即加駢檢校工部尚書，復鎮安南。

translations.literal: The emperor received their memorial, was greatly pleased, immediately promoted Pian to honorary Minister of Works, and restored him as governor of Annam.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received their report and was delighted; he immediately promoted Pian to honorary Minister of Works and restored him to command in Annam.

sentences.zh: 駢至海門而還。

translations.literal: Pian reached Haimen and turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Pian reached Haimen and turned back.

sentences.zh: 王晏權暗懦，動稟李維周之命；

translations.literal: Wang Yanquan was dull and timid; in every move he awaited Li Weizhou's orders;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanquan was dim-witted and timid; every move awaited Li Weizhou's word;

sentences.zh: 維周凶貪，諸將不為之用，遂解重圍，蠻遁去者太半。

translations.literal: Weizhou was vicious and greedy; the generals would not serve under him, so the tight siege was lifted and more than half the barbarians escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhou was brutal and grasping; the generals would not obey him, the siege slackened, and more than half the enemy slipped away.

sentences.zh: 駢至，復督勵將士攻城，遂克之，殺段酋遷及土蠻為南詔鄉導者朱道古，斬首三萬餘級，南詔遁去。

translations.literal: When Pian arrived he again roused the troops to assault the city and took it; he killed Duan Qiouqian and the native chieftain Zhu Daogu who had guided Nanzhao, beheaded more than thirty thousand, and Nanzhao fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Pian arrived he rallied the troops, stormed the city, and took it. He killed Duan Qiouqian and the native chieftain Zhu Daogu, who had guided Nanzhao, took more than thirty thousand heads, and Nanzhao withdrew.

sentences.zh: 駢又破土蠻附南詔者二洞，誅其酋長，土蠻帥眾歸附者萬七千人。

translations.literal: Pian also broke two caves of native tribes that had joined Nanzhao, executed their chiefs, and seventeen thousand native tribesmen submitted with their leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Pian also overran two native strongholds that had sided with Nanzhao, executed their chiefs, and received the submission of seventeen thousand tribesmen under their leaders.

sentences.zh: 十一月，壬子，赦天下。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, on renzi: amnesty for the empire.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on the day renzi, a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 詔安南、邕州、西川諸軍各保疆域，勿復進攻南詔。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the armies of Annam, Yong Prefecture, and West Sichuan each to hold their territories and not again advance against Nanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commanded the armies of Annam, Yongzhou, and West Sichuan to hold their own ground and make no further attacks on Nanzhao.

sentences.zh: 委劉潼曉諭，如能更修舊好，一切不問。

translations.literal: Liu Tong was entrusted to explain clearly: if they would restore the old friendship, all would be overlooked.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tong was charged to make clear that if Nanzhao would renew the old friendship, all past offenses would be forgiven.

sentences.zh: 置靜海軍於安南，以高駢為節度使。

translations.literal: The Jinghai Army was established at Annam, with Gao Pian as military governor.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinghai Army was established at Annam, with Gao Pian as its military governor.

sentences.zh: 自李涿侵擾群蠻，為安南患殆將十年，至是始平。

translations.literal: Since Li Zhuo had harassed the various tribes, the Annam troubles had lasted nearly ten years; only now were they pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Since Li Zhuo had stirred up the tribal peoples, Annam had been in turmoil for nearly ten years; only now was the region finally pacified.

sentences.zh: 駢築安南城，週三千步，造屋四十餘萬間。

translations.literal: Pian built Annam city with a circuit of three thousand paces and erected more than four hundred thousand buildings.
translations.idiomatic: Pian built the city of Annam with walls three thousand paces around and put up more than four hundred thousand structures.

sentences.zh: 十二月，黠戛斯遣將軍乙支連幾入貢，奏遣鞍馬迎冊立使及請亥年歷日。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: Kirghiz sent General Yizhi Lianji with tribute, memorializing to dispatch saddled horses to meet the investiture envoy and requesting the calendar for the hai year.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Kirghiz sent General Yizhi Lianji with tribute, asking that saddled horses be sent to meet the investiture envoy and requesting the calendar for the hai year.

sentences.zh: 以成德留後王景崇為節度使。

translations.literal: Wang Jingchong, acting governor of Chengde, was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingchong, acting governor of Chengde, was confirmed as military governor.

sentences.zh: 上好音樂宴游，殿前供奉樂工常近五百人，每月宴設不減十餘，水陸皆備，聽樂觀優，不知厭倦，賜與動及千緡。

translations.literal: The emperor loved music and feasting; palace musicians in attendance numbered nearly five hundred; each month there were no fewer than a dozen banquets, with provisions on land and water; he listened to music and watched entertainers without tiring; rewards often reached a thousand strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loved music and revelry. Nearly five hundred palace musicians stood ready before the hall; each month saw no fewer than a dozen feasts, with delicacies from land and sea. He listened to music and watched players without ever growing weary, and his gifts often ran to a thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 曲江，昆明、灞滻、南宮、北苑、昭應、咸陽，所欲游幸即行，不待供置，有司常具音樂、飲食、幄帟，諸王立馬以備陪從。

translations.literal: Qujiang, Kunming, Bahao, Southern Palace, Northern Park, Zhaoying, Xianyang—wherever he wished to tour he went at once, without waiting for preparations; the relevant offices always kept music, food, drink, and tents ready; the princes stood by with their horses to accompany him.
translations.idiomatic: Qujiang, Kunming Lake, Bahao, the Southern Palace, the Northern Park, Zhaoying, Xianyang—wherever he wished to go he went at once, without waiting for arrangements. The responsible offices always kept music, food, drink, and tents on hand, and the princes held their horses ready to ride along.

sentences.zh: 每行幸，內外諸司扈從者十餘萬人，所費不可勝紀。

translations.literal: On each tour, more than a hundred thousand from offices within and without the palace accompanied him; the expense was beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: On each outing more than a hundred thousand officials and attendants from within and outside the palace followed in his train, at a cost beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 懿宗昭聖恭惠孝皇帝上咸通八年（

translations.literal: Above: Emperor Yizong, the Sagely, Respectful, and Gracious Filial Emperor; eighth year of Xiantong (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yizong, the Sagely, Respectful, and Gracious Filial Emperor; eighth year of Xiantong (

sentences.zh: 丁亥，公元八六七年）

translations.literal: dinghai, AD 867)
translations.idiomatic: dinghai, AD 867)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，以魏博留後何全皞為節度使。

translations.literal: Spring, first month: He Quanhao, acting governor of Weibo, was made military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, He Quanhao, acting governor of Weibo, was appointed military governor.

sentences.zh: 二月，歸義節度使張義潮入朝，以為右神武統軍，命其族子惟深守歸義。

translations.literal: Second month: Zhang Yichao, military governor of Guiyi, entered court and was made commander of the Right Divine Martial Army; his clansman Weishen was ordered to hold Guiyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Zhang Yichao of Guiyi came to court and was made commander of the Right Divine Martial Army, while his kinsman Weishen was left to guard Guiyi.

sentences.zh: 自安南至邕、廣，海路多潛石覆舟，靜海節度使高駢募工鑿之，漕運無滯。

translations.literal: From Annam to Yong and Guang, the sea route had many hidden rocks that capsized ships; Jinghai military governor Gao Pian recruited workers to cut them away, and grain transport went unimpeded.
translations.idiomatic: Between Annam and Yong and Guang, hidden reefs wrecked many ships. Gao Pian, governor of Jinghai, hired workers to clear them, and the grain route ran smoothly again.

sentences.zh: 四川近邊六姓蠻，常持兩端，無寇則稱效順，有寇必為前鋒。

translations.literal: The Six-Clan tribes along the Sichuan frontier often kept both sides open: when there was no raid they claimed loyalty, but when there was a raid they always served as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: The Six-Clan tribes on the Sichuan frontier habitually played both sides—declaring loyalty in peace but leading the charge whenever raiders struck.

sentences.zh: 卑籠部獨盡心於唐，與群蠻為仇，朝廷賜姓李，除為刺史。

translations.literal: The Bilong tribe alone gave its full loyalty to Tang, made enemies of the other tribes, was granted the surname Li by the court, and was appointed prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Bilong tribe remained wholly loyal to Tang and feuded with the other tribes; the court granted them the surname Li and appointed their leader prefect.

sentences.zh: 節度使劉潼遣將將兵助之，討六姓蠻，焚其部落，斬首五千餘級。

translations.literal: Military governor Liu Tong sent generals with troops to assist them, attacked the Six-Clan tribes, burned their settlements, and took more than five thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Liu Tong sent troops to aid them, attacked the Six-Clan tribes, burned their camps, and took more than five thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 樂工李可及善為新聲，三月，上以可及為左威衛將軍。

translations.literal: The musician Li Keji was skilled at new music; in the third month the emperor made Keji a general of the Left Weiwu Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The musician Li Keji excelled at new compositions; in the third month the emperor made him a general of the Left Weiwu Guard.

sentences.zh: 曹確諫曰：「太宗定文武官六百餘員，謂房玄齡曰『朕以待天下賢士，工商雜流，不可處也。』

translations.literal: Cao Que remonstrated: "Emperor Taizong fixed more than six hundred civil and military posts and said to Fang Xuanling, 'I wait upon worthy men of the realm; merchants, craftsmen, and mixed professions must not hold office.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Que protested: "Emperor Taizong set more than six hundred civil and military posts and told Fang Xuanling, 'I reserve office for the worthy of the realm—merchants, artisans, and mixed professions must not hold rank.

sentences.zh: 大和中，文宗欲以樂工尉遲璋為王府率，拾遺竇洵直諫，即改光州長史。

translations.literal: In the Dahe era, Emperor Wenzong wished to make the musician Yuchi Zhang commandant of the princely household; remonstrance official Dou Xunzhi protested, and Zhang was immediately changed to long history of Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wenzong in the Dahe era, when the emperor wished to make the musician Yuchi Zhang commandant of the princely household, remonstrance official Dou Xunzhi objected and Zhang was promptly reassigned as long history of Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乞以兩朝故事，別除可及官。」

translations.literal: I beg that, following the precedents of both reigns, Keji be given a separate appointment."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Keji be given a different office, following the precedent of both earlier reigns."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，上不豫，群臣希進見。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: the emperor was unwell, and the ministers rarely gained audience.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, the emperor fell ill and the ministers seldom saw him.

sentences.zh: 五月，丙辰，疏理天下系囚，非臣蠹不可赦者，皆遞降一等。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on bingchen: prisoners under detention throughout the realm were reviewed; except for those who were irredeemable pests to the state, all had their sentences reduced one degree.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on bingchen, prisoners empire-wide were reviewed; all except irredeemable criminals had their sentences reduced by one degree.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，壬寅，蘄王緝薨。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, on renyin: Prince of Qi, Ji, died.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on renyin, Prince Ji of Qi died.

sentences.zh: 懷州民訴旱，刺史劉仁規揭榜禁之，民怒，相與作亂，逐仁規，仁規逃匿村舍。

translations.literal: The people of Huai Prefecture petitioned about drought; Prefect Liu Rengui posted a proclamation forbidding it. The people were angry, rose together in disorder, drove Rengui out, and Rengui fled and hid in a village house.
translations.idiomatic: When the people of Huai Prefecture petitioned about drought, Prefect Liu Rengui posted a ban on such complaints. Enraged, they rioted, drove him out, and he fled to hide in a village.

sentences.zh: 民入州宅，掠其家貲，登樓擊鼓，久之乃定。

translations.literal: The people entered the prefectural residence, plundered his household goods, climbed the tower and beat the drum; only after a long while did calm return.
translations.idiomatic: They stormed the prefectural compound, looted his property, climbed the tower and beat the drum, and order was restored only after a long while.

sentences.zh: 甲子，以兵部侍郎、充諸道鹽鐵轉運等使、附馬都尉-{于}-琮同平章事。

translations.literal: On jiazi, Vice Minister of War, Commissioner for Salt, Iron, and Transport of all circuits, and Imperial Son-in-Law Yu Zong were made Co-Directors of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, Vice Minister of War and Commissioner for Salt, Iron, and Transport Yu Zong, an imperial son-in-law, was made Co-Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 宣歙察使楊收過華岳廟，施衣物，使巫祈禱，縣令誣以為收罪。

translations.literal: Xuan-She observation commissioner Yang Shou passed Mount Hua's temple, bestowed clothing, and had shamans pray; the county magistrate falsely charged this as Shou's crime.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shou, observation commissioner of Xuan-She, visited Mount Hua's temple, gave offerings of clothing, and had shamans pray; the county magistrate falsely made this a charge against him.

sentences.zh: 右拾罪韋保衡復言，收前為相，除嚴譔江西節度使，受錢百萬，又置造船務，人訟其侵隱。

translations.literal: Right remonstrance official Wei Baoheng spoke again: when Shou had been chancellor he appointed Yan Zan military governor of Jiangxi and accepted a million in cash; he also established a shipbuilding office, and people sued him for embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: Right remonstrance official Wei Baoheng added that when Shou was chancellor he had appointed Yan Zan governor of Jiangxi for a million in cash, set up a shipbuilding office, and was accused of embezzlement.

sentences.zh: 八月，庚寅，貶收端州司馬。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on gengyin: Shou was demoted to army supervisor of Duan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on gengyin, Shou was demoted to army supervisor of Duan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 九月，上疾瘳。

translations.literal: Ninth month: the emperor's illness abated.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the emperor recovered from his illness.

sentences.zh: 冬，十二月，信王心丐薨。

translations.literal: Winter, twelfth month: Prince of Xin, Xingai, died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the twelfth month, Prince Xingai of Xin died.

sentences.zh: 加嶺南東道節度使韋宙同平章事。

translations.literal: Wei Zhou, military governor of Lingnan East Circuit, was additionally made Co-Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhou, military governor of Lingnan East Circuit, was also made Co-Director of the Secretariat.
